<file path="app/Imports/WarehouseImport.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Imports;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\Warehouse;
  6: use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
  7: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
  8: use Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\ToCollection;
  9: use Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\WithHeadingRow;
 10: 
 11: /**
 12:  * Imports warehouse items from an Excel file.
 13:  *
 14:  * TWO MODES
 15:  * ---------
 16:  * The caller chooses how an EXISTING item's quantity is handled when the
 17:  * same (garage_id, code) pair appears in the spreadsheet:
 18:  *
 19:  *   - OVERWRITE (default): the new quantity REPLACES the stored one.
 20:  *     Use this when the Excel file represents the garage's current,
 21:  *     authoritative inventory snapshot.
 22:  *
 23:  *   - ADD: the new quantity is ADDED to the stored one.
 24:  *     Use this when the Excel file contains newly received parts and
 25:  *     the warehouse already holds some units of the same code.
 26:  *     Example: 500 L in stock + 2000 L arriving → 2500 L total.
 27:  *
 28:  * In both modes, name/unit/price/supplier are updated to the Excel
 29:  * values when the row exists — the operator's latest catalog metadata
 30:  * always wins.
 31:  *
 32:  * Duplicate codes INSIDE the same file are handled correctly: the
 33:  * second occurrence of a code updates the in-memory result of the
 34:  * first (via the DB), so both modes behave consistently.
 35:  */
 36: class WarehouseImport extends AbstractImport implements ToCollection, WithHeadingRow
 37: {
 38:     /**
 39:      * How to treat the quantity of an existing item.
 40:      */
 41:     public const MODE_OVERWRITE = 'overwrite';
 42: 
 43:     public const MODE_ADD = 'add';
 44: 
 45:     /**
 46:      * @param  int|null  $garageId  Positive for tenant imports.
 47:      * @param  int|null  $companyId  Optional, used for strict company scoping.
 48:      * @param  string  $mode  One of MODE_OVERWRITE or MODE_ADD.
 49:      */
 50:     public function __construct(
 51:         ?int $garageId = null,
 52:         ?int $companyId = null,
 53:         public readonly string $mode = self::MODE_OVERWRITE,
 54:     ) {
 55:         parent::__construct($garageId, $companyId);
 56: 
 57:         if (! in_array($mode, [self::MODE_OVERWRITE, self::MODE_ADD], true)) {
 58:             throw new \InvalidArgumentException(sprintf(
 59:                 'WarehouseImport: unknown mode [%s]. Expected [%s] or [%s].',
 60:                 $mode,
 61:                 self::MODE_OVERWRITE,
 62:                 self::MODE_ADD,
 63:             ));
 64:         }
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     public function collection(Collection $rows): void
 68:     {
 69:         foreach ($rows as $row) {
 70:             $code = trim((string) ($row['code'] ?? $row['kod'] ?? ''));
 71:             $name = trim((string) ($row['name'] ?? $row['ad'] ?? ''));
 72:             $quantity = (int) ($row['quantity'] ?? $row['miqdar'] ?? 0);
 73:             $unit = $row['unit'] ?? $row['olcu_vahidi'] ?? null;
 74: 
 75:             $rawPrice = $row['price'] ?? $row['qiymet'] ?? '0';
 76:             $price = $this->parsePrice($rawPrice);
 77: 
 78:             if (empty($code) || empty($name)) {
 79:                 $this->recordSkip(
 80:                     $this->nextRowIndex(),
 81:                     $code ?: '—',
 82:                     empty($code)
 83:                         ? __('messages.imports.reasons.name_empty')
 84:                         : __('messages.imports.reasons.name_empty')
 85:                 );
 86: 
 87:                 continue;
 88:             }
 89: 
 90:             DB::transaction(function () use ($code, $name, $quantity, $unit, $price): void {
 91:                 // Searching without global scopes is required to detect a
 92:                 // soft-deleted row. Lock it before reading its quantity so
 93:                 // simultaneous additive imports cannot lose stock.
 94:                 $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
 95:                     ->where('garage_id', $this->garageId)
 96:                     ->where('code', $code)
 97:                     ->lockForUpdate()
 98:                     ->first();
 99: 
100:                 if ($warehouse) {
101:                     if ($warehouse->trashed()) {
102:                         $warehouse->restore();
103:                     }
104: 
105:                     $newQuantity = $this->mode === self::MODE_ADD
106:                         ? $warehouse->quantity + $quantity
107:                         : $quantity;
108: 
109:                     $warehouse->update([
110:                         'name' => $name,
111:                         'quantity' => $newQuantity,
112:                         'unit' => $unit,
113:                         'price' => $price,
114:                     ]);
115: 
116:                     return;
117:                 }
118: 
119:                 Warehouse::create([
120:                     'code' => $code,
121:                     'name' => $name,
122:                     'quantity' => $quantity,
123:                     'unit' => $unit,
124:                     'price' => $price,
125:                     'garage_id' => $this->garageId,
126:                     'company_id' => $this->companyId,
127:                 ]);
128:             });
129: 
130:             $this->incrementImported();
131:         }
132:     }
133: 
134:     /**
135:      * Parse a price value from an Excel cell.
136:      *
137:      * Handles the two common locale formats:
138:      *   - AZ / TR: "1.500,50"  → 1500.50   (nöqtə minliklər, vergül onluq)
139:      *   - US / EN: "1,500.50"  → 1500.50   (vergül minliklər, nöqtə onluq)
140:      *   - Plain:   "1500.50"   → 1500.50
141:      *              "1500,50"   → 1500.50
142:      *
143:      * Strategiya: hər iki ayırıcı varsa, SONUNCU olan onluq ayırıcıdır.
144:      * Yalnız biri varsa, 2 rəqəmdən sonra gəlirsə onluq, əks halda minlik
145:      * sayılır.
146:      */
147:     private function parsePrice(mixed $raw): float
148:     {
149:         if ($raw === null || $raw === '') {
150:             return 0.0;
151:         }
152: 
153:         $value = trim((string) $raw);
154: 
155:         // Bütün boşluq / valyuta simvollarını sil (₼, $, €, AZN və s.)
156:         $value = preg_replace('/[^\d.,\-]/u', '', $value);
157: 
158:         if ($value === '' || $value === '-') {
159:             return 0.0;
160:         }
161: 
162:         $hasDot = str_contains($value, '.');
163:         $hasComma = str_contains($value, ',');
164: 
165:         if ($hasDot && $hasComma) {
166:             // Sonuncu ayırıcı onluq ayırıcıdır.
167:             $lastDot = strrpos($value, '.');
168:             $lastComma = strrpos($value, ',');
169: 
170:             if ($lastComma > $lastDot) {
171:                 // "1.500,50" → 1500.50
172:                 $value = str_replace('.', '', $value);
173:                 $value = str_replace(',', '.', $value);
174:             } else {
175:                 // "1,500.50" → 1500.50
176:                 $value = str_replace(',', '', $value);
177:             }
178:         } elseif ($hasComma) {
179:             // Yalnız vergül: "1500,50" → 1500.50 ; "1,500" → 1500
180:             $pos = strrpos($value, ',');
181:             $decimals = strlen($value) - $pos - 1;
182: 
183:             if ($decimals === 3 && $pos > 0) {
184:                 // "1,500" → minliklər
185:                 $value = str_replace(',', '', $value);
186:             } else {
187:                 // "1500,50" → onluq
188:                 $value = str_replace(',', '.', $value);
189:             }
190:         }
191:         // Yalnız nöqtə varsa və ya heç biri yoxdursa — olduğu kimi qalır.
192: 
193:         return (float) $value;
194:     }
195: }
</file>

 61: 
 62:     /**

 68:     {
 69:         return $this->hasOne(BusDailyStatus::class)->latestOfMany('date');
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     /**
 73:      * Daily distance driven — the difference between the two most
 74:      * recent KM records for this bus.
 75:      *
 76:      * Returns null when there are fewer than 2 records (no baseline
 77:      * for comparison). The value is clamped at 0 because a stationary

 79:      * "0 km", never as a negative number.
 80:      *
 81:      * IMPORTANT: callers should eager-load the `dailyKmRecords`
 82:      * relation with `->limit(2)` to avoid an N+1 query on list pages.
 83:      */
 84:     public function getDailyKmAttribute(): ?int
 85:     {
 86:         $records = $this->relationLoaded('dailyKmRecords')
 87:             ? $this->dailyKmRecords->take(2)
 88:             : $this->dailyKmRecords()->take(2)->get();
 89: 
 90:         if ($records->count() < 2) {
 91:             return null;
 92:         }
 93: 
 94:         return max(0, $records[0]->km - $records[1]->km);
 95:     }
 96: 
 97:     public function scopeActive($query)
 98:     {
 99:         return $query->where('is_active', true);
100:     }
101: 
102:     public function scopeInactive($query)
103:     {
104:         return $query->where('is_active', false);
105:     }
106: 
107:     public function oilChanges()
108:     {
109:         return $this->hasMany(BusOilChange::class)->orderByDesc('actual_km');
110:     }
111: 
112:     public function latestOilChange(OilType|string $type)
113:     {
114:         $value = $type instanceof OilType ? $type->value : $type;
115: 
116:         return $this->hasOne(BusOilChange::class)
117:             ->where('oil_type', $value)
118:             ->latestOfMany('actual_km');
119:     }
120: 
121:     // ==================== EAGER-LOADABLE LATEST RELATIONS ====================
122:     //
123:     // These three relations exist specifically so that list pages
124:     // (DashboardController::computeOilChangeData and
125:     // OilChangeController::buildStatusRows) can eager-load the MOST
126:     // RECENT oil change per (bus, oil_type) pair in three queries
127:     // total — instead of loading the entire oil-change history with
128:     // `with('oilChanges')`, which grows linearly with fleet size ×
129:     // history depth.
130:     //
131:     // Before: 500 buses × ~50 history rows = ~25,000 models in memory.
132:     // After:  500 buses × 3 types            =  ~1,500 models in memory.
133:     //
134:     // `latestOilChange($type)` still exists for one-off lookups on a
135:     // single bus (e.g. the show page). All four paths share the same
136:     // `latestOfMany('actual_km')` subquery, so the returned model is
137:     // identical regardless of which one is used.
138: 
139:     public function latestMotorOilChange()
140:     {
141:         return $this->hasOne(BusOilChange::class)
142:             ->where('oil_type', OilType::Motor->value)
143:             ->latestOfMany('actual_km');
144:     }
145: 
146:     public function latestGearboxOilChange()
147:     {
148:         return $this->hasOne(BusOilChange::class)
149:             ->where('oil_type', OilType::Gearbox->value)
150:             ->latestOfMany('actual_km');
151:     }
152: 
153:     public function latestAxleOilChange()
154:     {
155:         return $this->hasOne(BusOilChange::class)
156:             ->where('oil_type', OilType::Axle->value)
157:             ->latestOfMany('actual_km');
158:     }
159: 
160:     public function motorOilIntervalKm(): int
161:     {
162:         $threshold = (int) config('oil.bus_length_threshold', 15);
163:         $isLarge = ((float) ($this->uzunluq ?? 12)) >= $threshold;
164: 
165:         $key = $isLarge ? '18m' : '12m';
166: 
167:         return (int) config("oil.intervals.motor.{$key}", 36000);
168:     }
169: 
170:     public function axleOilIntervalKm(): int
171:     {
172:         return (int) config('oil.intervals.axle.default', 180000);
173:     }
174: 
175:     public static function gearboxIntervalForBrand(?string $brand): int
176:     {
177:         $intervals = config('oil.intervals.gearbox', []);
178:         $default = (int) ($intervals['default'] ?? 180000);
179: 
180:         if ($brand === null || $brand === '') {
181:             return $default;
182:         }
183: 
184:         return (int) ($intervals[$brand] ?? $default);
185:     }
186: 
187:     public function nextOilIntervalKm(OilType $type): int
188:     {
189:         return match ($type) {
190:             OilType::Motor => $this->motorOilIntervalKm(),
191:             OilType::Axle => $this->axleOilIntervalKm(),
192:             OilType::Gearbox => self::gearboxIntervalForBrand(
193:                 $this->latestOilChange(OilType::Gearbox)?->oil_brand
194:             ),
195:         };
196:     }
197: }

<file path="app/Models/BusOilChange.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Models;
  4: 
  5: use App\Enums\OilType;
  6: use App\Models\Traits\Auditable;
  7: use App\Models\Traits\HasCreatedBy;
  8: use App\Models\Traits\HasGarageScope;
  9: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
 10: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
 11: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
 12: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
 13: 
 14: class BusOilChange extends Model
 15: {
 16:     use Auditable, HasCreatedBy, HasFactory, HasGarageScope, SoftDeletes;
 17: 
 18:     protected $fillable = [
 19:         'bus_id',
 20:         'oil_type',
 21:         'oil_brand',
 22:         'scheduled_km',
 23:         'actual_km',
 24:         'interval_km',
 25:         'changed_at',
 26:         'notes',
 27:         'garage_id',
 28:         'company_id',
 29:     ];
 30: 
 31:     protected $casts = [
 32:         'oil_type' => OilType::class,
 33:         'scheduled_km' => 'integer',
 34:         'actual_km' => 'integer',
 35:         'interval_km' => 'integer',
 36:         'changed_at' => 'date',
 37:     ];
 38: 
 39:     public function bus()
 40:     {
 41:         return $this->belongsTo(Bus::class);
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     public function scopeOfType(Builder $query, OilType|string $type): Builder
 45:     {
 46:         $value = $type instanceof OilType ? $type->value : $type;
 47: 
 48:         return $query->where('oil_type', $value);
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     public function scopeLatestFirst(Builder $query): Builder
 52:     {
 53:         return $query->orderByDesc('actual_km')->orderByDesc('id');
 54:     }
 55: 
 56:     /**
 57:      * Determine the interval to use for the NEXT oil change of the given
 58:      * type for the given bus.
 59:      *
 60:      * Priority:
 61:      *   1. The bus's own history — median of consecutive gaps
 62:      *   2. Config fallback — motor: length, gearbox: brand, axle: fixed
 63:      */
 64:     public static function effectiveIntervalFor(Bus $bus, OilType $type): int
 65:     {
 66:         // Get last 4 changes so we can compute up to 3 deltas.
 67:         $kms = static::withoutGlobalScopes()
 68:             ->where('bus_id', $bus->id)
 69:             ->where('oil_type', $type->value)
 70:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 71:             ->orderByDesc('actual_km')
 72:             ->limit(4)
 73:             ->pluck('actual_km')
 74:             ->map(fn ($v) => (int) $v)
 75:             ->values()
 76:             ->all();
 77: 
 78:         // ─── Derive from history ───
 79:         if (count($kms) >= 2) {
 80:             $deltas = [];
 81: 
 82:             for ($i = 0; $i < count($kms) - 1; $i++) {
 83:                 $delta = $kms[$i] - $kms[$i + 1];
 84: 
 85:                 if ($delta > 0) {
 86:                     $deltas[] = $delta;
 87:                 }
 88:             }
 89: 
 90:             if (! empty($deltas)) {
 91:                 sort($deltas);
 92: 
 93:                 // Median is more robust than avg — ignores one-off outliers.
 94:                 return $deltas[(int) floor(count($deltas) / 2)];
 95:             }
 96:         }
 97: 
 98:         // ─── Fallback to config ───
 99:         return match ($type) {
100:             OilType::Motor => $bus->motorOilIntervalKm(),
101:             OilType::Axle => $bus->axleOilIntervalKm(),
102:             OilType::Gearbox => Bus::gearboxIntervalForBrand(
103:                 static::withoutGlobalScopes()
104:                     ->where('bus_id', $bus->id)
105:                     ->where('oil_type', OilType::Gearbox->value)
106:                     ->whereNull('deleted_at')
107:                     ->orderByDesc('actual_km')
108:                     ->value('oil_brand')
109:             ),
110:         };
111:     }
112: 
113:     public function nextDueKm(): int
114:     {
115:         return $this->actual_km + $this->interval_km;
116:     }
117: }
</file>

<file path="app/Models/ComplaintDetail.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Models;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\Traits\Auditable;
  6: use App\Models\Traits\HasGarageScope;
  7: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
  8: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
  9: 
 10: class ComplaintDetail extends Model
 11: {
 12:     use Auditable, HasGarageScope, SoftDeletes;
 13: 
 14:     /**
 15:      * Fields excluded from audit logging.
 16:      *
 17:      * `stock_quantity` — this is a snapshot of the warehouse quantity
 18:      * at the time the detail was created. It changes automatically
 19:      * whenever a part is used and is not meaningful for auditing.
 20:      * Operators care about `used_quantity`, not the running balance.
 21:      */
 22:     protected static array $auditExcluded = [
 23:         'stock_quantity',
 24:         'price_at_use',
 25:     ];
 26: 
 27:     protected $fillable = [
 28:         'complaint_id',
 29:         'shikayet_index',
 30:         'code',
 31:         'name',
 32:         'stock_quantity',
 33:         'used_quantity',
 34:         'price_at_use',   // ← YENİ
 35:         'source_type',
 36:         'employee_id',
 37:         'notes',
 38:         'garage_id',
 39:         'company_id',
 40:     ];
 41: 
 42:     public function complaint()
 43:     {
 44:         return $this->belongsTo(Complaint::class);
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     /**
 48:      * The employee that performed this work.
 49:      *
 50:      * Uses withTrashed() because a complaint detail is a HISTORICAL
 51:      * record — an employee who later leaves the company (and is
 52:      * soft-deleted) must still render their original name on every
 53:      * past complaint. This mirrors ComplaintPdfService::generate(),
 54:      * which already resolves soft-deleted employees so that the
 55:      * generated PDF matches what the show page displays.
 56:      *
 57:      * HasGarageScope remains active, so a cross-tenant reference
 58:      * (which should not exist, but is protected against anyway)
 59:      * still cannot leak an employee from another garage.
 60:      */
 61:     public function employee()
 62:     {
 63:         return $this->belongsTo(Employee::class)->withTrashed();
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     /**
 67:      * True when the stock for this detail came from a service
 68:      * vehicle instead of the garage warehouse.
 69:      */
 70:     public function isFromServiceVehicle(): bool
 71:     {
 72:         return $this->source_type === 'service_vehicle';
 73:     }
 74: 
 75:     public function isFromWarehouse(): bool
 76:     {
 77:         return $this->source_type === 'warehouse';
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     /**
 81:      * True when this detail was imported as historical data — it never
 82:      * touched stock, and delete/update operations must leave stock
 83:      * untouched.
 84:      */
 85:     public function isHistorical(): bool
 86:     {
 87:         return $this->source_type === 'historical';
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     /**
 91:      * True when this detail represents an inspection or repair that
 92:      * did NOT consume any stock (used_quantity = 0). The row is kept
 93:      * for documentation so future operators can see that the part was
 94:      * looked at, without polluting the stock ledger.
 95:      */
 96:     public function isInspection(): bool
 97:     {
 98:         return $this->source_type === 'inspection';
 99:     }
100: 
101:     /**
102:      * True when this detail actually consumed stock. Used by report
103:      * queries that need to exclude inspection/historical rows.
104:      */
105:     public function consumedStock(): bool
106:     {
107:         return in_array($this->source_type, ['warehouse', 'service_vehicle'], true)
108:             && $this->used_quantity > 0;
109:     }
110: 
111:     /**
112:      * Total cost of this detail line — used_quantity × price_at_use.
113:      *
114:      * Returns null when the price snapshot is unknown (legacy historical
115:      * rows, or rows where the warehouse price was NULL at the time of use).
116:      */
117:     public function getTotalCostAttribute(): ?float
118:     {
119:         if ($this->price_at_use === null) {
120:             return null;
121:         }
122: 
123:         return (float) $this->used_quantity * (float) $this->price_at_use;
124:     }
125: }

<file path="app/Models/ComplaintItem.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Models;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Traits\Auditable;
 6: use App\Models\Traits\HasGarageScope;
 7: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
 8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 9: 
10: class ComplaintItem extends Model
11: {
12:     use Auditable, HasGarageScope;
13: 
14:     protected $fillable = [
15:         'complaint_id',
16:         'description',
17:         'type',
18:         'garage_id',
19:         'company_id',
20:     ];
21: 
22:     // ==================== RELATIONS ====================
23: 
24:     public function complaint()
25:     {
26:         return $this->belongsTo(Complaint::class);
27:     }
28: 
29:     // ==================== SCOPES ====================
30: 
31:     /**
32:      * Find recurring complaints on the same bus.
33:      *
34:      * A complaint is considered "recurring" if:
35:      *  - within the last $days days on the same bus,
36:      *  - with the same description,
37:      *  - at least twice,
38:      *  - and not yet in "completed" status.
39:      *
40:      * The manual `where('complaints.garage_id', ...)` filter has been
41:      * removed — HasGarageScope now applies it automatically on the
42:      * `complaint_items` table itself. This makes the scope bulletproof
43:      * even if a future refactor drops the explicit join condition.
44:      *
45:      * @return \Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder
46:      */
47:     public function scopeRecurring($query, int $days = 30)
48:     {
49:         // Defense-in-depth: this scope has no meaning without a garage
50:         // context. HasGarageScope deliberately disables itself in the
51:         // console (including PHPUnit), so relying on it alone would let
52:         // a missing context return cross-tenant data. We block explicitly.
53:         $garageId = \App\Services\GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
54: 
55:         if (! $garageId) {
56:             return $query->whereRaw('1 = 0');
57:         }
58: 
59:         return $query
60:             ->select(
61:                 'complaint_items.description',
62:                 'complaints.bus_id',
63:                 DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total'),
64:                 DB::raw('MAX(complaints.created_at) as last_occurrence')
65:             )
66:             ->join('complaints', 'complaints.id', '=', 'complaint_items.complaint_id')
67:             ->whereNull('complaints.deleted_at')
68:             ->where('complaints.created_at', '>=', now()->subDays($days))
69:             ->where(function ($q) {
70:                 $q->where('complaints.status', '!=', \App\Enums\ComplaintStatus::Completed->value)
71:                     ->orWhereNull('complaints.status');
72:             })
73:             ->groupBy('complaint_items.description', 'complaints.bus_id')
74:             ->havingRaw('COUNT(*) >= 2')
75:             ->orderByDesc('total');
76:     }
77: }
</file>

14:

16:         'code',

33:         if (empty($this->last_name)) {
34:             return $this->first_name;

40:     /**
41:      * Human-readable display name with position label.
42:      *
43:      * The `position` column stores a config key (e.g. "master",
44:      * "electrician"), not the label shown to users. The label lives
45:      * in config('settings.employee_positions') so that admins can
46:      * update the wording without a migration.
47:      *
48:      * Resolving the label here means every consumer — the complaint
49:      * form's employee dropdown, the show page detail rows, the PDF
50:      * act, and every report — displays the same friendly label
51:      * ("🔧 Master") instead of the raw key ("master").
52:      *
53:      * Unknown keys (custom positions typed directly into the DB)
54:      * fall through unchanged, preserving the previous behavior.
55:      *
56:      * @return string e.g. "Əli Məmmədov (🔧 Master)"
57:      */
58:     public function getFullNameWithPositionAttribute(): string
59:     {
60:         $name = $this->first_name;
61: 
62:         if (! empty($this->last_name)) {
63:             $name .= ' '.$this->last_name;
64:         }
65: 
66:         $positionKey = trim((string) $this->position);
67: 
68:         if ($positionKey === '') {
69:             return $name;
70:         }
71: 
72:         $labels = config('settings.employee_positions', []);
73:         $positionLabel = $labels[$positionKey] ?? $positionKey;
74: 
75:         return $name.' ('.$positionLabel.')';
76:     }
77: 
78:     // ==================== RELATIONSHIPS ====================
79:     public function complaints()
80:     {
81:         return $this->hasMany(Complaint::class);
82:     }
83:

87:         return $query->where('is_active', true);
88:     }
89: }

<file path="app/Models/Traits/Auditable.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Models\Traits;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\AuditLog;
  6: use App\Services\GarageContext;
  7: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
  8: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
  9: 
 10: trait Auditable
 11: {
 12:     protected static array $auditBaseExcludedFields = [
 13:         'password',
 14:         'remember_token',
 15:         'created_at',
 16:         'updated_at',
 17:         'deleted_at',
 18:     ];
 19: 
 20:     protected static function bootAuditable(): void
 21:     {
 22:         // Create event
 23:         static::created(function (Model $model) {
 24:             $newValues = static::filterAuditValues($model->getAttributes());
 25: 
 26:             if (empty($newValues)) {
 27:                 return;
 28:             }
 29: 
 30:             $model->writeAudit('created', null, $newValues);
 31:         });
 32: 
 33:         // Update event — only after successful save
 34:         static::updated(function (Model $model) {
 35:             $newValues = static::filterAuditValues($model->getChanges());
 36: 
 37:             if (empty($newValues)) {
 38:                 return;
 39:             }
 40: 
 41:             $oldValues = array_intersect_key(
 42:                 static::filterAuditValues($model->getOriginal()),
 43:                 $newValues
 44:             );
 45: 
 46:             $model->writeAudit('updated', $oldValues, $newValues);
 47:         });
 48: 
 49:         // Delete event — soft delete or force delete
 50:         static::deleted(function (Model $model) {
 51:             $isForceDelete = method_exists($model, 'isForceDeleting')
 52:                 && $model->isForceDeleting();
 53: 
 54:             $model->writeAudit(
 55:                 $isForceDelete ? 'force_deleted' : 'deleted',
 56:                 static::filterAuditValues($model->getOriginal()),
 57:                 null
 58:             );
 59:         });
 60: 
 61:         // Restore event.
 62:         //
 63:         // IMPORTANT: `restored()` is defined on the SoftDeletes trait, NOT
 64:         // on Model. Calling `static::restored(...)` on a model that does
 65:         // not use SoftDeletes would fall through to Model::__callStatic,
 66:         // which constructs a NEW model instance to proxy the call. Since
 67:         // this boot method runs from inside `bootIfNotBooted()`, creating
 68:         // a new instance re-enters `bootIfNotBooted()` while the model is
 69:         // still booting, and PHP throws a LogicException.
 70:         //
 71:         // Guard the registration so it only runs when SoftDeletes is
 72:         // actually in use.
 73:         if (static::usesSoftDeletes()) {
 74:             static::restored(function (Model $model) {
 75:                 $model->writeAudit(
 76:                     'restored',
 77:                     ['deleted_at' => $model->getOriginal('deleted_at')],
 78:                     ['deleted_at' => null]
 79:                 );
 80:             });
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     /**
 85:      * Determine whether the current model uses the SoftDeletes trait.
 86:      */
 87:     protected static function usesSoftDeletes(): bool
 88:     {
 89:         return in_array(
 90:             SoftDeletes::class,
 91:             class_uses_recursive(static::class),
 92:             true
 93:         );
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     protected static function filterAuditValues(array $values): array
 97:     {
 98:         $excluded = static::$auditBaseExcludedFields;
 99: 
100:         if (property_exists(static::class, 'auditExcluded')) {
101:             $excluded = array_merge($excluded, static::$auditExcluded);
102:         }
103: 
104:         return array_diff_key($values, array_flip($excluded));
105:     }
106: 
107:     protected function writeAudit(string $event, ?array $oldValues, ?array $newValues): void
108:     {
109:         AuditLog::create([
110:             'user_id' => auth()->id(),
111:             'garage_id' => $this->resolveAuditGarageId(),
112:             'company_id' => $this->resolveAuditCompanyId(),
113:             'auditable_type' => get_class($this),
114:             'auditable_id' => $this->getKey(),
115:             'event' => $event,
116:             'old_values' => $oldValues,
117:             'new_values' => $newValues,
118:         ]);
119:     }
120: 
121:     /**
122:      * Resolve the garage_id to associate with this audit log.
123:      *
124:      * Default: the model's own garage_id attribute if present,
125:      * falling back to the current request's garage context.
126:      *
127:      * Models that do not have a `garage_id` attribute but represent
128:      * a garage themselves (e.g. the Garage model) override this
129:      * method to return their own primary key.
130:      */
131:     protected function resolveAuditGarageId(): ?int
132:     {
133:         if (! empty($this->garage_id)) {
134:             return (int) $this->garage_id;
135:         }
136: 
137:         return GarageContext::getGarageId();
138:     }
139: 
140:     /**
141:      * Resolve the company_id to associate with this audit log.
142:      *
143:      * Default: the model's own company_id attribute if present,
144:      * falling back to the current request's company context.
145:      *
146:      * The Company model overrides this to return its own primary key.
147:      */
148:     protected function resolveAuditCompanyId(): ?int
149:     {
150:         if (! empty($this->company_id)) {
151:             return (int) $this->company_id;
152:         }
153: 
154:         return GarageContext::getCompanyId();
155:     }
156: 
157:     /**
158:      * Write a single audit log entry per record for a bulk update.
159:      */
160:     public static function auditBulkUpdate(
161:         array $ids,
162:         array $newValues,
163:         string $event = 'bulk_updated'
164:     ): void {
165:         $newValues = static::filterAuditValues($newValues);
166: 
167:         if (empty($newValues)) {
168:             return;
169:         }
170: 
171:         $oldRecords = static::whereIn('id', $ids)->get()->keyBy('id');
172: 
173:         foreach ($oldRecords as $id => $oldRecord) {
174:             $oldArray = static::filterAuditValues($oldRecord->getOriginal());
175: 
176:             $changed = [];
177:             foreach ($newValues as $key => $value) {
178:                 $oldValue = $oldArray[$key] ?? null;
179: 
180:                 if (static::valuesDiffer($oldValue, $value)) {
181:                     $changed[$key] = $value;
182:                 }
183:             }
184: 
185:             if (empty($changed)) {
186:                 continue;
187:             }
188: 
189:             AuditLog::create([
190:                 'user_id' => auth()->id(),
191:                 'garage_id' => $oldRecord->resolveAuditGarageId(),
192:                 'company_id' => $oldRecord->resolveAuditCompanyId(),
193:                 'auditable_type' => static::class,
194:                 'auditable_id' => $id,
195:                 'event' => $event,
196:                 'old_values' => array_intersect_key($oldArray, $changed),
197:                 'new_values' => $changed,
198:             ]);
199:         }
200:     }
201: 
202:     /**
203:      * Write one audit log entry per record for a bulk delete.
204:      */
205:     public static function auditBulkDelete(
206:         array $ids,
207:         string $event = 'bulk_deleted'
208:     ): void {
209:         if (empty($ids)) {
210:             return;
211:         }
212: 
213:         $oldRecords = static::whereIn('id', $ids)->get();
214: 
215:         foreach ($oldRecords as $oldRecord) {
216:             AuditLog::create([
217:                 'user_id' => auth()->id(),
218:                 'garage_id' => $oldRecord->resolveAuditGarageId(),
219:                 'company_id' => $oldRecord->resolveAuditCompanyId(),
220:                 'auditable_type' => static::class,
221:                 'auditable_id' => $oldRecord->getKey(),
222:                 'event' => $event,
223:                 'old_values' => static::filterAuditValues($oldRecord->getOriginal()),
224:                 'new_values' => null,
225:             ]);
226:         }
227:     }
228: 
229:     public function auditLogs()
230:     {
231:         return $this->morphMany(AuditLog::class, 'auditable');
232:     }
233: 
234:     // ==================== VALUE COMPARISON ====================
235: 
236:     protected static function valuesDiffer(mixed $old, mixed $new): bool
237:     {
238:         return static::normalizeForComparison($old)
239:             !== static::normalizeForComparison($new);
240:     }
241: 
242:     protected static function normalizeForComparison(mixed $value): mixed
243:     {
244:         if ($value === null) {
245:             return null;
246:         }
247: 
248:         if (is_bool($value)) {
249:             return $value ? '1' : '0';
250:         }
251: 
252:         if (is_array($value) || is_object($value)) {
253:             return $value;
254:         }
255: 
256:         return (string) $value;
257:     }
258: }

<file path="app/Models/Traits/HasGarageScope.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Models\Traits;
  4: 
  5: use App\Exceptions\MissingGarageContextException;
  6: use App\Services\GarageContext;
  7: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
  8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context;
  9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
 10: 
 11: trait HasGarageScope
 12: {
 13:     protected static function bootHasGarageScope(): void
 14:     {
 15:         // ==================== GLOBAL SCOPE ====================
 16:         static::addGlobalScope('garage', function (Builder $builder) {
 17:             $garageId = GarageContext::getGarageId();
 18: 
 19:             if ($garageId) {
 20:                 $builder->where(
 21:                     $builder->getModel()->getTable().'.garage_id',
 22:                     $garageId
 23:                 );
 24: 
 25:                 return;
 26:             }
 27: 
 28:             // No context — allow console commands (migrations, seeders, tinker)
 29:             // and queue workers to run without a garage filter. Web requests
 30:             // should ALWAYS have a context set by the middleware stack; if they
 31:             // reach here without one it means the middleware was bypassed, so
 32:             // we return zero rows (fail-closed) to prevent cross-tenant leaks.
 33:             if (app()->runningInConsole()) {
 34:                 return;
 35:             }
 36: 
 37:             // HTTP request with no garage context → return no rows.
 38:             $builder->whereRaw('1 = 0');
 39:         });
 40: 
 41:         // ==================== CREATING EVENT ====================
 42:         static::creating(function ($model) {
 43:             // If garage_id is already set, don't touch it (manual override).
 44:             if ($model->garage_id !== null) {
 45:                 return;
 46:             }
 47: 
 48:             // Resolve via the centralized chain:
 49:             // Context → session → auth user → null.
 50:             $garageId = GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
 51:             $companyId = GarageContext::resolveCompanyId();
 52: 
 53:             if ($garageId !== null) {
 54:                 $model->garage_id = $garageId;
 55:                 $model->company_id = $companyId;
 56: 
 57:                 return;
 58:             }
 59: 
 60:             // No context available — defer the decision to the handler.
 61:             self::handleMissingGarageContext($model);
 62:         });
 63: 
 64:         // ==================== COMPANY_ID CONSISTENCY GUARD ====================
 65:         // company_id must always match the garage's company. If a caller
 66:         // provided a mismatched company_id, silently correct it to prevent
 67:         // data corruption.
 68:         static::creating(function ($model) {
 69:             if ($model->garage_id && $model->company_id) {
 70:                 $garageCompanyId = \App\Models\Garage::withoutGlobalScopes()
 71:                     ->whereKey($model->garage_id)
 72:                     ->value('company_id');
 73: 
 74:                 if ($garageCompanyId && (int) $model->company_id !== (int) $garageCompanyId) {
 75:                     $attempted = $model->company_id;
 76:                     $model->company_id = $garageCompanyId;
 77: 
 78:                     Log::warning('HasGarageScope: corrected mismatched company_id', [
 79:                         'model' => get_class($model),
 80:                         'garage_id' => $model->garage_id,
 81:                         'attempted' => $attempted,
 82:                         'corrected' => $garageCompanyId,
 83:                     ]);
 84:                 }
 85:             }
 86:         });
 87:     }
 88: 
 89:     /**
 90:      * No garage context found — block the operation.
 91:      *
 92:      * Behavior by environment:
 93:      *   - Real console (migration, seeder, tinker): continue silently.
 94:      *     Operators running those commands explicitly control the DB.
 95:      *   - Everywhere else — including unit tests and web requests —
 96:      *     throw MissingGarageContextException. The exception is caught
 97:      *     by bootstrap/app.php and either returns JSON or redirects
 98:      *     the user to garage selection.
 99:      *
100:      * Reasoning: silently writing `garage_id = NULL` creates ghost
101:      * rows invisible to all garages and all reports. It is always
102:      * preferable to fail loudly.
103:      */
104:     protected static function handleMissingGarageContext($model): void
105:     {
106:         // Real console (NOT tests): continue silently.
107:         //
108:         // Note: PHPUnit tests also run in console, so we must
109:         // additionally check runningUnitTests() to distinguish the
110:         // two. Without it, every test would skip this guard.
111:         if (app()->runningInConsole() && ! app()->runningUnitTests()) {
112:             return;
113:         }
114: 
115:         // Log before throwing — helps diagnosis even when the exception
116:         // is caught and converted into a user-facing redirect.
117:         Log::error('Garage context missing — blocking write', [
118:             'model' => get_class($model),
119:             'attributes' => collect($model->getAttributes())
120:                 ->except(['password', 'remember_token'])
121:                 ->toArray(),
122:             'request_id' => Context::get('request_id'),
123:             'user_id' => auth()->id(),
124:             'url' => request()?->fullUrl(),
125:         ]);
126: 
127:         throw new MissingGarageContextException(get_class($model));
128:     }
129: 
130:     // ==================== RELATIONS ====================
131: 
132:     public function garage()
133:     {
134:         return $this->belongsTo(\App\Models\Garage::class);
135:     }
136: 
137:     public function company()
138:     {
139:         return $this->belongsTo(\App\Models\Company::class);
140:     }
141: }
</file>

 23:     /**

 25:      *
 26:      * The layout calls isDirector() on every request to decide the
 27:      * sidebar/topbar rendering. Without cache, that's one DB query
 28:      * per call. The cache resets when the model is rehydrated.
 29:      *
 30:      * null  = not yet computed
 31:      * true  = user is an active director
 32:      * false = user is not a director
 33:      */

 36:     /**
 37:      * Per-instance cache for hasGarageRole() results.
 38:      *
 39:      * The sidebar layout calls hasGarageRole() 5-6 times per request
 40:      * to decide which menu sections to render. Without this cache
 41:      * every call fires its own EXISTS query against the pivot table.
 42:      *
 43:      * Key: "garageId:role1|role2|..." — the exact tuple asked for.
 44:      * Value: true/false.
 45:      *
 46:      * @var array<string, bool>
 47:      */
 48:     private array $cachedGarageRoles = [];

 50:     /**

 53:      * Called after any pivot change on company_user or garage_user
 54:      * when the same User instance will be inspected again within the
 55:      * same request.
 56:      */
 57:     public function forgetRoleCache(): static
 58:     {
 59:         $this->cachedIsDirector = null;
 60:         $this->cachedGarageRoles = [];
 61: 
 62:         return $this;
 63:     }
 64: 
 65:     /**

 67:      *
 68:      * The sidebar layout and PostLoginRedirector call isDirector()
 69:      * on every request. When a caller mutates the `company_user`
 70:      * pivot on this same instance (assign / remove / change director),
 71:      * it must call this method so the next isDirector() check sees
 72:      * the new state instead of the cached value.
 73:      *
 74:      * Kept separate from forgetRoleCache() so a caller who only
 75:      * touched company-level data does not need to invalidate the
 76:      * (potentially expensive to rebuild) garage-role cache.
 77:      */

 79:     {
 80:         $this->cachedIsDirector = null;
 81: 
 82:         return $this;
 83:     }

 88:      * NOTE: 'role' is intentionally NOT fillable. It must be set explicitly
 89:      * via promoteToSuperAdmin() / demoteToRegularUser() helpers, or via
 90:      * forceFill(['role' => ...]) in trusted contexts (seeders, factories).
 91:      *
 92:      * This prevents privilege escalation through mass assignment payloads
 93:      * such as POST ['role' => 'super_admin'].
 94:      */

149:         'two_factor_recovery_codes',
150:     ];

153:         'email_verified_at' => 'datetime',

156:         'two_factor_recovery_codes' => 'encrypted:array',
157:         'two_factor_confirmed_at' => 'datetime',

161: 
162:     public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
163:     {
164:         return $this->role === 'super_admin';
165:     }
166: 
167:     public function isRegularUser(): bool
168:     {
169:         return $this->role === 'user';
170:     }
171: 
172:     // ==================== GARAGE-LEVEL ROLE CHECKS ====================
173: 
174:     /**
175:      * True when the user holds one of the given roles in the given
176:      * garage (or the current one). Result is cached per instance, so
177:      * the sidebar's 5-6 permission checks per page load cost one
178:      * query each and no more.
179:      */
180:     public function hasGarageRole(string|array $roles, ?int $garageId = null): bool
181:     {
182:         $roles = (array) $roles;
183:         $garageId ??= GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
184: 
185:         if (! $garageId) {
186:             return false;
187:         }
188: 
189:         // Canonical cache key — sort the roles so [a, b] and [b, a]
190:         // share a cache entry.
191:         $sortedRoles = $roles;
192:         sort($sortedRoles);
193:         $cacheKey = $garageId.':'.implode('|', $sortedRoles);
194: 
195:         if (array_key_exists($cacheKey, $this->cachedGarageRoles)) {
196:             return $this->cachedGarageRoles[$cacheKey];
197:         }
198: 
199:         $result = $this->garages()
200:             ->whereKey($garageId)
201:             ->wherePivot('is_active', true)
202:             ->wherePivotIn('role', $roles)
203:             ->exists();
204: 
205:         $this->cachedGarageRoles[$cacheKey] = $result;
206: 
207:         return $result;
208:     }
209: 
210:     /**
211:      * Invalidate the per-instance hasGarageRole() cache.
212:      *
213:      * Call this after mutating the garage_user pivot on the same
214:      * instance (UserManagementController, UserService) so the next
215:      * permission check sees the new state.
216:      */
217:     public function forgetGarageRoleCache(): static
218:     {
219:         $this->cachedGarageRoles = [];
220: 
221:         return $this;
222:     }

418: 
419:     /**
420:      * Verify a TOTP code against this user's secret.
421:      *
422:      * REPLAY DEFENSE
423:      * --------------
424:      * A TOTP code is valid for a sliding window of ±30 seconds (see
425:      * TwoFactorManager::verifyCode, window: 1). Without a replay
426:      * guard the same 6-digit code could be reused inside that window
427:      * — an attacker who captures a code via network sniffing,
428:      * shoulder-surfing, or a compromised browser session could log
429:      * in a second time after the legitimate user has already done so.
430:      *
431:      * We mark every accepted code in the cache for 120 seconds — the
432:      * widest possible window in which a code could still be valid.
433:      * Once marked, the same code is rejected for the rest of its
434:      * lifetime. A fresh code (30 seconds later) gets a new cache key
435:      * and works normally.
436:      *
437:      * The cache key includes the user id so two users whose secrets
438:      * happen to produce the same 6-digit value at the same instant do
439:      * not block each other.
440:      */
441:     public function verifyTwoFactorCode(string $code): bool
442:     {
443:         if (! $this->two_factor_secret) {
444:             return false;
445:         }
446: 
447:         // Quick syntactical guard before touching the cache.
448:         if (! preg_match('/^\d{6}$/', $code)) {
449:             return false;
450:         }
451: 
452:         $cacheKey = 'totp_used:'.$this->getKey().':'.hash('sha256', $code);
453: 
454:         // Already consumed inside the acceptance window → reject.
455:         if (Cache::has($cacheKey)) {
456:             return false;
457:         }
458: 
459:         $valid = app(TwoFactorManager::class)->verifyCode(
460:             $this->two_factor_secret,
461:             $code,
462:         );
463: 
464:         if ($valid) {
465:             // 120 seconds covers the widest possible TOTP window
466:             // (30s current step + 30s past + 30s future) with a
467:             // 30-second safety margin. After that the code cannot
468:             // be reused anyway because it has naturally expired.
469:             Cache::put($cacheKey, true, now()->addSeconds(120));
470:         }
471: 
472:         return $valid;
473:     }
474: 
475:     /**
476:      * Verify a recovery code. On success, the used code is removed
477:      * from the stored list (one-time use).
478:      *
479:      * Defensive: if the value came back as a JSON string (this can happen
480:      * if the `encrypted:array` cast was not applied for any reason — a
481:      * stale model instance, a missing cast, or data written before the
482:      * cast existed), decode it inline so the operation still works.
483:      */
484:     public function useRecoveryCode(string $code): bool
485:     {
486:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($code) {
487:             // Re-fetch the row with a pessimistic lock. Without this,
488:             // two concurrent requests can both read the SAME list of
489:             // codes, both find a match, and both succeed — each one
490:             // consuming a different "slot" but the same physical code.
491:             //
492:             // `lockForUpdate()` serializes the two requests: the second
493:             // one blocks until the first commits, then re-reads the
494:             // already-updated list and correctly rejects the reused
495:             // code.
496:             //
497:             // We deliberately use `static::query()` instead of
498:             // `withoutGlobalScopes()` — the User model only registers
499:             // the SoftDeletes global scope, so a plain query preserves
500:             // it and correctly excludes soft-deleted accounts. A
501:             // soft-deleted user must never be able to consume a
502:             // recovery code.
503:             $fresh = static::query()
504:                 ->whereKey($this->getKey())
505:                 ->lockForUpdate()
506:                 ->first();
507: 
508:             if (! $fresh) {
509:                 return false;
510:             }
511: 
512:             $codes = $fresh->two_factor_recovery_codes ?? [];
513: 
514:             // Defensive: allow JSON-encoded string fallback.
515:             if (is_string($codes)) {
516:                 $codes = json_decode($codes, true) ?? [];
517:             }
518: 
519:             if (! is_array($codes)) {
520:                 return false;
521:             }
522: 
523:             foreach ($codes as $index => $hashedCode) {
524:                 if (Hash::check($code, $hashedCode)) {
525:                     unset($codes[$index]);
526: 
527:                     $fresh->forceFill([
528:                         'two_factor_recovery_codes' => array_values($codes),
529:                     ])->save();
530: 
531:                     // Keep the caller's in-memory instance consistent
532:                     // with the freshly persisted row.
533:                     $this->setRawAttributes($fresh->getAttributes(), true);
534: 
535:                     return true;
536:                 }
537:             }
538: 
539:             return false;
540:         });
541:     }
542: }
</file>

193:      */
194:     public function getDestinationLabelFullAttribute(): string

196:         if ($this->type instanceof TransferType && $this->type->isReturnToQuarantine()) {
197:             return __('messages.transfers.destination_quarantine');
198:         }
199: 
200:         return $this->destination_label;
201:     }
202: 
203:     /**
204:      * True for transfers that do NOT go through the full
205:      * draft → dispatch → receive workflow.
206:      */
207:     public function isImmediate(): bool
208:     {
209:         return $this->type instanceof TransferType
210:             && ! $this->type->requiresWorkflow();
211:     }

<file path="app/Observers/UserObserver.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Observers;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\User;
 6: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context;
 7: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
 8: 
 9: /**
10:  * User model observer.
11:  *
12:  * Revokes every active API token the moment an account transitions
13:  * from active (is_active = true) to deactivated (is_active = false).
14:  *
15:  * WHY THIS EXISTS
16:  * ---------------
17:  * SuperAdmin\UserController already revokes tokens inline when it
18:  * flips the is_active flag, but relying on every caller to remember
19:  * that step is fragile: a future bulk-update action, a console
20:  * command, or a data migration could set is_active = false without
21:  * going through that controller, leaving the API tokens alive.
22:  *
23:  * Moving the revocation into a model observer makes the invariant
24:  * hold for EVERY code path that touches the is_active column
25:  * through Eloquent — not just the one controller written today.
26:  */
27: class UserObserver
28: {
29:     /**
30:      * Handle the User "updated" event.
31:      */
32:     public function updated(User $user): void
33:     {
34:         // Only act on an is_active change.
35:         if (! $user->wasChanged('is_active')) {
36:             return;
37:         }
38: 
39:         // getOriginal() still returns the pre-update value here —
40:         // syncOriginal() runs AFTER the updated event is dispatched.
41:         $wasActive = (bool) $user->getOriginal('is_active');
42:         $isNowActive = (bool) $user->is_active;
43: 
44:         // Only revoke on the active → inactive transition.
45:         if (! ($wasActive && ! $isNowActive)) {
46:             return;
47:         }
48: 
49:         $revokedCount = $user->tokens()->count();
50: 
51:         if ($revokedCount === 0) {
52:             return;
53:         }
54: 
55:         $user->tokens()->delete();
56: 
57:         Log::warning('API tokens revoked after user deactivation', [
58:             'user_id' => $user->id,
59:             'revoked_count' => $revokedCount,
60:             'deactivated_by' => auth()->id(),
61:             'request_id' => Context::get('request_id'),
62:         ]);
63:     }
64: }

<file path="app/Policies/UserPolicy.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Policies;
 4: 
 5: use App\Enums\RoleEnum;
 6: use App\Models\User;
 7: use App\Services\GarageContext;
 8: 
 9: class UserPolicy
10: {
11:     public function viewAny(User $user): bool
12:     {
13:         return $user->isSuperAdmin()
14:             || $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value);
15:     }
16: 
17:     public function view(User $user, User $targetUser): bool
18:     {
19:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
20:             return true;
21:         }
22: 
23:         if (! $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)) {
24:             return false;
25:         }
26: 
27:         return $this->targetSharesCurrentGarage($targetUser);
28:     }
29: 
30:     public function create(User $user): bool
31:     {
32:         return $user->isSuperAdmin()
33:             || $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value);
34:     }
35: 
36:     public function update(User $user, ?User $targetUser = null): bool
37:     {
38:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
39:             return true;
40:         }
41: 
42:         if (! $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)) {
43:             return false;
44:         }
45: 
46:         if ($targetUser === null) {
47:             return true;
48:         }
49: 
50:         return $this->targetSharesCurrentGarage($targetUser);
51:     }
52: 
53:     public function delete(User $user, User $targetUser): bool
54:     {
55:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
56:             return true;
57:         }
58: 
59:         if (! $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)) {
60:             return false;
61:         }
62: 
63:         return $this->targetSharesCurrentGarage($targetUser);
64:     }
65: 
66:     private function targetSharesCurrentGarage(User $targetUser): bool
67:     {
68:         $garageId = GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
69: 
70:         if (! $garageId) {
71:             return false;
72:         }
73: 
74:         return $targetUser->garages()
75:             ->whereKey($garageId)
76:             ->exists();
77:     }
78: }

<file path="app/Policies/WarehouseTransferPolicy.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Policies;
  4: 
  5: use App\Enums\RoleEnum;
  6: use App\Models\User;
  7: use App\Models\WarehouseTransfer;
  8: use App\Services\GarageContext;
  9: 
 10: class WarehouseTransferPolicy
 11: {
 12:     public function viewAny(User $user): bool
 13:     {
 14:         return $user->isSuperAdmin()
 15:             || $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value);
 16:     }
 17: 
 18:     public function view(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 19:     {
 20:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 21:             return true;
 22:         }
 23: 
 24:         if (! $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)) {
 25:             return false;
 26:         }
 27: 
 28:         $garageId = GarageContext::getGarageId();
 29: 
 30:         return $transfer->isSource($garageId) || $transfer->isDestination($garageId);
 31:     }
 32: 
 33:     public function create(User $user): bool
 34:     {
 35:         return $user->isSuperAdmin()
 36:             || $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value);
 37:     }
 38: 
 39:     public function dispatch(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 40:     {
 41:         // Status check runs for EVERY user, including SuperAdmin.
 42:         if (! $transfer->status->isDraft()) {
 43:             return false;
 44:         }
 45: 
 46:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 47:             return true;
 48:         }
 49: 
 50:         return $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)
 51:             && $transfer->isSource(GarageContext::getGarageId());
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     public function receive(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 55:     {
 56:         if (! $transfer->status->isDispatched()) {
 57:             return false;
 58:         }
 59: 
 60:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 61:             return true;
 62:         }
 63: 
 64:         return $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)
 65:             && $transfer->isDestination(GarageContext::getGarageId());
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     public function reject(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 69:     {
 70:         return $this->receive($user, $transfer);
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     public function resolve(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 74:     {
 75:         if (! $transfer->status->isDisputed()) {
 76:             return false;
 77:         }
 78: 
 79:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 80:             return true;
 81:         }
 82: 
 83:         return $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)
 84:             && $transfer->isSource(GarageContext::getGarageId());
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     public function cancel(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
 88:     {
 89:         if (! $transfer->status->isDraft()) {
 90:             return false;
 91:         }
 92: 
 93:         if ($user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 94:             return true;
 95:         }
 96: 
 97:         return $user->hasGarageRole(RoleEnum::ADMIN->value)
 98:             && $transfer->isSource(GarageContext::getGarageId());
 99:     }
100: 
101:     public function delete(User $user, WarehouseTransfer $transfer): bool
102:     {
103:         return $this->cancel($user, $transfer);
104:     }
105: }

 22:     {
 23:         //
 24:     }

 27:     {

 32:         }

 37:                 : Password::min(8);

 44:         \Illuminate\Support\Facades\View::composer(
 45:             'layouts.app',
 46:             PendingTransferComposer::class,
 47:         );
 48:         $this->registerRateLimiters();
 49:         $this->registerSuperAdminAuthListeners();
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     /**
 53:      * Log every successful and failed authentication involving the
 54:      * SuperAdmin account.
 55:      *
 56:      * The SuperAdmin is the single most privileged account on the
 57:      * platform. Even without MFA, emitting a `warning`-level log line
 58:      * on every SuperAdmin login (success OR failure) gives operators
 59:      * an immediate signal in monitoring tools if the account is being
 60:      * attacked or used unexpectedly.
 61:      *
 62:      * We use `warning` rather than `info` so the entries surface in
 63:      * production logs without lowering the log level.
 64:      */
 65:     protected function registerSuperAdminAuthListeners(): void
 66:     {
 67:         Event::listen(Login::class, function (Login $event) {
 68:             if (! $event->user instanceof User) {
 69:                 return;
 70:             }
 71: 
 72:             if (! $event->user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 73:                 return;
 74:             }
 75: 
 76:             Log::warning('SuperAdmin logged in', [
 77:                 'user_id' => $event->user->id,
 78:                 'email' => $event->user->email,
 79:                 'ip' => request()?->ip(),
 80:                 'user_agent' => request()?->userAgent(),
 81:                 'request_id' => \Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context::get('request_id'),
 82:             ]);
 83:         });
 84: 
 85:         Event::listen(Failed::class, function (Failed $event) {
 86:             $email = $event->credentials['email'] ?? null;
 87: 
 88:             if (! is_string($email) || $email === '') {
 89:                 return;
 90:             }
 91: 
 92:             // Look up the user to determine if the target is a SuperAdmin.
 93:             // This does NOT leak information back to the caller — the
 94:             // response to the user is identical regardless.
 95:             $user = User::where('email', $email)->first();
 96: 
 97:             if (! $user || ! $user->isSuperAdmin()) {
 98:                 return;
 99:             }
100: 
101:             Log::warning('Failed SuperAdmin login attempt', [
102:                 'email' => $email,
103:                 'ip' => request()?->ip(),
104:                 'user_agent' => request()?->userAgent(),
105:                 'request_id' => \Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context::get('request_id'),
106:             ]);
107:         });
108:     }
109: 
110:     /**
111:      * Named rate limiters — `throttle:<name>` middleware vasitəsilə işlədilir.
112:      */
113:     protected function registerRateLimiters(): void
114:     {
115:         RateLimiter::for('login', function (Request $request) {
116:             [$attempts, $decayMinutes] = $this->parseRateLimit('login');
117: 
118:             return Limit::perMinutes($decayMinutes, $attempts)
119:                 ->by(strtolower((string) $request->input('email')).'|'.$request->ip());
120:         });
121: 
122:         RateLimiter::for('api', function (Request $request) {
123:             [$attempts, $decayMinutes] = $this->parseRateLimit('api');
124: 
125:             return Limit::perMinutes($decayMinutes, $attempts)
126:                 ->by($request->user()?->id ?: $request->ip());
127:         });
128: 
129:         RateLimiter::for('pdf', function (Request $request) {
130:             [$attempts, $decayMinutes] = $this->parseRateLimit('pdf');
131: 
132:             return Limit::perMinutes($decayMinutes, $attempts)
133:                 ->by($request->user()?->id ?: $request->ip());
134:         });
135: 
136:         RateLimiter::for('import', function (Request $request) {
137:             [$attempts, $decayMinutes] = $this->parseRateLimit('import');
138: 
139:             return Limit::perMinutes($decayMinutes, $attempts)
140:                 ->by($request->user()?->id ?: $request->ip());
141:         });
142: 
143:         RateLimiter::for('lookup', function (Request $request) {
144:             [$attempts, $decayMinutes] = $this->parseRateLimit('lookup');
145: 
146:             return Limit::perMinutes($decayMinutes, $attempts)
147:                 ->by($request->user()?->id ?: $request->ip());
148:         });
149:     }
150: 
151:     /**
152:      * @return array{0: int, 1: int}
153:      */
154:     protected function parseRateLimit(string $name): array
155:     {
156:         $raw = (string) config("rate_limits.{$name}", '60,1');
157:         $parts = array_map('trim', explode(',', $raw));
158: 
159:         $attempts = max(1, (int) ($parts[0] ?? 60));
160:         $decayMinutes = max(1, (int) ($parts[1] ?? 1));
161: 
162:         return [$attempts, $decayMinutes];
163:     }
164: }

<file path="app/Services/BusService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\Bus;
  6: use Illuminate\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator;
  7: 
  8: class BusService
  9: {
 10:     /**
 11:      * Eager-load set shared by the two paginated list methods.
 12:      *
 13:      * NOTE ON `dailyKmRecords`
 14:      * ------------------------
 15:      * The `dailyKmRecords` relation is intentionally NOT eager-loaded
 16:      * here. The previous implementation used:
 17:      *
 18:      *     'dailyKmRecords' => fn ($q) => $q->limit(2)
 19:      *
 20:      * which is a well-known Laravel footgun: the `limit(2)` is added
 21:      * to the eager-load subquery, so PostgreSQL returns 2 rows TOTAL
 22:      * for all buses — not 2 rows per bus. With 25 buses on a page,
 23:      * only the first bus received its records; every other bus got
 24:      * an empty collection, and Bus::getDailyKmAttribute() returned
 25:      * null, so the "Daily KM" column rendered "—" for 24 of 25 rows.
 26:      *
 27:      * Laravel has no native "limit N per parent" eager-loading. The
 28:      * correct approaches are:
 29:      *
 30:      *   1. Use hasOne()->latestOfMany() for a single row per parent
 31:      *      (this is how latestKmRecord works).
 32:      *   2. Let the accessor query per-bus (N+1) when the eager-loaded
 33:      *      data is not available.
 34:      *   3. Install a package like staudenmeir/eloquent-eager-limit.
 35:      *
 36:      * We chose (2) here: the accessor's fallback path is a per-bus
 37:      * query scoped to the current model, which is correct. The cost
 38:      * is at most one query per bus on the page (≤ 25 by default),
 39:      * each of them indexed on (bus_id, date) and returning at most 2
 40:      * rows. That is a small price for correct output.
 41:      *
 42:      * @return array<int|string, mixed>
 43:      */
 44:     private function busListWith(): array
 45:     {
 46:         return [
 47:             'brand',
 48:             'latestKmRecord',
 49:         ];
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     public function getPaginatedBuses(?string $search = null, int $perPage = 15): LengthAwarePaginator
 53:     {
 54:         $query = Bus::with($this->busListWith());
 55: 
 56:         if ($search) {
 57:             $query->where(function ($q) use ($search) {
 58:                 $q->where('dqn', 'ILIKE', "%{$search}%")
 59:                     ->orWhere('route_number', 'ILIKE', "%{$search}%")
 60:                     ->orWhere('bus_project', 'ILIKE', "%{$search}%");
 61:             });
 62:         }
 63: 
 64:         return $query->orderBy('id', 'desc')->paginate($perPage);
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     public function advancedSearch(array $filters, int $perPage = 15): LengthAwarePaginator
 68:     {
 69:         $query = Bus::with($this->busListWith());
 70: 
 71:         if (! empty($filters['brand_id'])) {
 72:             $query->where('brand_id', (int) $filters['brand_id']);
 73:         }
 74: 
 75:         // Text fields support a case-insensitive partial match through
 76:         // ILIKE. These columns are all varchar / text in PostgreSQL.
 77:         $textFields = [
 78:             'bus_project', 'vin', 'route_number', 'dqn', 'engine_number',
 79:         ];
 80: 
 81:         foreach ($textFields as $field) {
 82:             if (! empty($filters[$field])) {
 83:                 $query->where($field, 'ILIKE', '%'.$filters[$field].'%');
 84:             }
 85:         }
 86: 
 87:         // `uzunluq` is decimal(5,2). PostgreSQL rejects ILIKE on
 88:         // numeric columns with SQLSTATE 42883 ("operator does not
 89:         // exist: numeric ~~* unknown"), which used to surface as a
 90:         // 500 error every time the operator typed anything into the
 91:         // "Length..." filter field.
 92:         //
 93:         // We cast to text so the substring semantics match what the
 94:         // UI actually offers: the user types "12" and expects every
 95:         // bus whose length renders as "...12..." to appear.
 96:         if (! empty($filters['uzunluq'])) {
 97:             $query->whereRaw(
 98:                 'CAST(uzunluq AS TEXT) ILIKE ?',
 99:                 ['%'.$filters['uzunluq'].'%']
100:             );
101:         }
102: 
103:         return $query->orderBy('id', 'desc')->paginate($perPage);
104:     }
105: 
106:     public function createBus(array $data): Bus
107:     {
108:         $data['date'] = now()->format('Y-m-d');
109: 
110:         return Bus::create($data);
111:     }
112: 
113:     public function updateBus(Bus $bus, array $data): Bus
114:     {
115:         $bus->update($data);
116: 
117:         return $bus->fresh();
118:     }
119: 
120:     public function deleteBus(Bus $bus): void
121:     {
122:         $bus->delete();
123:     }
124: 
125:     /**
126:      * Bulk-update the active flag on multiple buses.
127:      *
128:      * IMPORTANT: the audit call MUST run BEFORE the actual DB update.
129:      * `auditBulkUpdate()` compares the requested new value against the
130:      * current value stored in the database. If we update first, the
131:      * comparison sees identical values and silently skips logging.
132:      *
133:      * Ids are processed in chunks so a 10 000-row selection does not
134:      * overflow PostgreSQL's parameter limit (65 535) nor time out
135:      * inside auditBulkUpdate's per-row INSERT loop.
136:      */
137:     public function bulkUpdateStatus(array $ids, bool $isActive): void
138:     {
139:         if (empty($ids)) {
140:             return;
141:         }
142: 
143:         $event = $isActive ? 'bulk_activated' : 'bulk_deactivated';
144: 
145:         foreach (array_chunk($ids, 500) as $chunk) {
146:             Bus::auditBulkUpdate($chunk, ['is_active' => $isActive], $event);
147: 
148:             Bus::whereIn('id', $chunk)->update(['is_active' => $isActive]);
149:         }
150:     }
151: 
152:     /**
153:      * Bulk soft-delete multiple buses.
154:      *
155:      * The audit snapshot must be taken before deletion so that the
156:      * original values are preserved in the audit log. Ids are
157:      * chunked for the same reason as bulkUpdateStatus().
158:      */
159:     public function bulkDelete(array $ids): void
160:     {
161:         if (empty($ids)) {
162:             return;
163:         }
164: 
165:         foreach (array_chunk($ids, 500) as $chunk) {
166:             Bus::auditBulkDelete($chunk);
167: 
168:             Bus::whereIn('id', $chunk)->delete();
169:         }
170:     }
171: 
172:     /**
173:      * Bulk soft-delete ALL buses matching the given filters.
174:      *
175:      * Ids are streamed from the database in chunks via cursor() so the
176:      * full list never lives in PHP memory. Each chunk is then deleted
177:      * through bulkDelete() so audit entries continue to be written.
178:      */
179:     public function bulkDeleteAllByFilters(array $filters): int
180:     {
181:         $query = Bus::query();
182: 
183:         if (! empty($filters['brand_id'])) {
184:             $query->where('brand_id', (int) $filters['brand_id']);
185:         }
186: 
187:         $searchableFields = [
188:             'bus_project', 'vin', 'uzunluq', 'route_number', 'dqn', 'engine_number',
189:         ];
190: 
191:         foreach ($searchableFields as $field) {
192:             if (! empty($filters[$field])) {
193:                 $query->where($field, 'ILIKE', '%'.$filters[$field].'%');
194:             }
195:         }
196: 
197:         $totalDeleted = 0;
198:         $buffer = [];
199: 
200:         foreach ($query->select('id')->cursor() as $row) {
201:             $buffer[] = $row->id;
202: 
203:             if (count($buffer) >= 500) {
204:                 $this->bulkDelete($buffer);
205:                 $totalDeleted += count($buffer);
206:                 $buffer = [];
207:             }
208:         }
209: 
210:         if (! empty($buffer)) {
211:             $this->bulkDelete($buffer);
212:             $totalDeleted += count($buffer);
213:         }
214: 
215:         return $totalDeleted;
216:     }
217: }
</file>

<file path="app/Services/Complaint/ComplaintItemService.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services\Complaint;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Complaint;
 6: use App\Models\ComplaintItem;
 7: 
 8: class ComplaintItemService
 9: {
10:     public function syncItems(Complaint $complaint, array $items, ?string $type): void
11:     {
12:         $validItems = array_values(array_filter(array_map('trim', $items)));
13:         $existingItems = $complaint->items()->orderBy('id')->get();
14: 
15:         foreach ($validItems as $index => $description) {
16:             if ($existingItems->has($index)) {
17:                 $item = $existingItems[$index];
18:                 if ($item->description !== $description || $item->type !== $type) {
19:                     $item->update([
20:                         'description' => $description,
21:                         'type' => $type,
22:                     ]);
23:                 }
24:             } else {
25:                 $complaint->items()->create([
26:                     'description' => $description,
27:                     'type' => $type,
28:                     // garage_id and company_id are set by HasGarageScope's
29:                     // creating event via GarageContext, but we pass them
30:                     // explicitly so the row is correct even when the
31:                     // calling code runs outside a normal web request
32:                     // (e.g. queue jobs, console imports).
33:                     'garage_id' => $complaint->garage_id,
34:                     'company_id' => $complaint->company_id,
35:                 ]);
36:             }
37:         }
38: 
39:         if ($existingItems->count() > count($validItems)) {
40:             $idsToDelete = $existingItems->slice(count($validItems))->pluck('id')->all();
41: 
42:             // IMPORTANT: `$complaint->items()->whereIn(...)->delete()`
43:             // would run as a Query Builder delete and skip Eloquent's
44:             // `deleted` event — meaning no audit log would be written.
45:             // We load the models and delete them one by one so the
46:             // Auditable trait fires for each row.
47:             ComplaintItem::whereIn('id', $idsToDelete)->get()->each->delete();
48:         }
49:     }
50: }

<file path="app/Services/Complaint/ComplaintPdfService.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services\Complaint;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Complaint;
 6: use App\Models\Employee;
 7: use Barryvdh\DomPDF\Facade\Pdf;
 8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
 9: 
10: class ComplaintPdfService
11: {
12:     private const PDF_DIR = 'akt';
13: 
14:     public function generate(Complaint $complaint): \Barryvdh\DomPDF\PDF
15:     {
16:         $complaint->loadMissing(['details.employee', 'bus', 'creator', 'closer', 'serviceVehicle']);
17: 
18:         // Collect every related employee id — both from details and
19:         // from the top-level employee_id field.
20:         $employeeIds = $complaint->details
21:             ->pluck('employee_id')
22:             ->filter()
23:             ->unique();
24: 
25:         if ($complaint->employee_id) {
26:             $employeeIds->push($complaint->employee_id);
27:         }
28: 
29:         // Filter by the complaint's own garage_id so a detail row that
30:         // (through an old bug or manual DB edit) references an employee
31:         // from another tenant cannot leak that employee's name into
32:         // the PDF. Soft-deleted employees are still resolved so
33:         // historical complaints render their original names.
34:         $employeesById = Employee::withoutGlobalScopes()
35:             ->where('garage_id', $complaint->garage_id)
36:             ->whereIn('id', $employeeIds->unique()->values())
37:             ->get()
38:             ->keyBy('id');
39: 
40:         return Pdf::loadView('complaints.akt', [
41:             'complaint' => $complaint,
42:             'company' => $complaint->company,
43:             'garage' => $complaint->garage,
44:             'employeesById' => $employeesById,
45:         ]);
46:     }
47: 
48:     public function save(Complaint $complaint): string
49:     {
50:         $pdf = $this->generate($complaint);
51:         $relativePath = self::PDF_DIR."/akt-{$complaint->id}.pdf";
52: 
53:         Storage::disk('local')->put($relativePath, $pdf->output());
54: 
55:         return Storage::disk('local')->path($relativePath);
56:     }
57: 
58:     public function getFilePath(Complaint $complaint): string
59:     {
60:         return Storage::disk('local')->path(
61:             self::PDF_DIR."/akt-{$complaint->id}.pdf"
62:         );
63:     }
64: 
65:     public function exists(Complaint $complaint): bool
66:     {
67:         return Storage::disk('local')->exists(
68:             self::PDF_DIR."/akt-{$complaint->id}.pdf"
69:         );
70:     }
71: 
72:     /**
73:      * Delete the PDF file for the given complaint.
74:      *
75:      * NOTE: This method deletes ONLY the generated PDF file, not the
76:      * complaint row. Complaint deletion lives in ComplaintService.
77:      *
78:      * ✅ P2 FIX: The old bulkDelete() method was removed because it
79:      * silently called this method inside a loop and returned a "deleted
80:      * count" that misleadingly looked like complaint-row deletions.
81:      * ComplaintService::bulkDelete() is the single source of truth.
82:      */
83:     public function delete(Complaint $complaint): bool
84:     {
85:         return Storage::disk('local')->delete(
