<file path="app/Services/Complaint/ComplaintService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\Complaint;
  4: 
  5: use App\Enums\ComplaintStatus;
  6: use App\Enums\Location;
  7: use App\Models\Complaint;
  8: use App\Models\ComplaintDetail;
  9: use App\Models\Driver;
 10: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context;
 11: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 12: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
 13: 
 14: class ComplaintService
 15: {
 16:     /**
 17:      * Resolved lazily in the constructor so tests that manually
 18:      * construct this service (without a PDF dependency) keep
 19:      * working. Production always goes through the container, which
 20:      * injects a real instance.
 21:      */
 22:     protected ComplaintPdfService $pdfService;
 23: 
 24:     public function __construct(
 25:         protected ComplaintStockService $stockService,
 26:         protected ComplaintItemService $itemService,
 27:         protected ComplaintStatusTransitionService $transitionService,
 28:         ?ComplaintPdfService $pdfService = null,
 29:     ) {
 30:         $this->pdfService = $pdfService ?? app(ComplaintPdfService::class);
 31:     }
 32: 
 33:     public function create(array $data, ?array $detallar = null, array $shikayet = []): Complaint
 34:     {
 35:         $this->applyLocationContext($data);
 36: 
 37:         $data['created_by'] = auth()->id();
 38: 
 39:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($data, $detallar, $shikayet) {
 40:             $processedDetails = [];
 41: 
 42:             if (! empty($detallar) && is_array($detallar)) {
 43:                 $location = ($data['yer'] ?? null) instanceof Location
 44:                     ? $data['yer']->value
 45:                     : ($data['yer'] ?? 'garage');
 46: 
 47:                 $processedDetails = $this->stockService->deductStock(
 48:                     $detallar,
 49:                     $location,
 50:                     $data['service_vehicle_id'] ?? null
 51:                 );
 52:             }
 53: 
 54:             $complaint = Complaint::create($data);
 55: 
 56:             if (! empty($processedDetails)) {
 57:                 $complaint->details()->createMany($processedDetails);
 58:             }
 59: 
 60:             $this->itemService->syncItems($complaint, $shikayet, $data['complaint_type'] ?? null);
 61: 
 62:             return $complaint;
 63:         });
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     public function update(Complaint $complaint, array $data, ?array $detallar = null, array $shikayet = []): Complaint
 67:     {
 68:         $this->applyLocationContext($data);
 69: 
 70:         $updated = DB::transaction(function () use ($complaint, $data, $detallar, $shikayet) {
 71:             // ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
 72:             // Lock the complaint row FIRST so concurrent updates on
 73:             // the same complaint are serialized. Without this, two
 74:             // admins editing the same card simultaneously each read
 75:             // the same "old" details, each compute a stock diff
 76:             // against those details, and each write back — corrupting
 77:             // the stock ledger with a double restore + double deduct.
 78:             $locked = Complaint::withoutGlobalScopes()
 79:                 ->whereKey($complaint->getKey())
 80:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 81:                 ->lockForUpdate()
 82:                 ->firstOrFail();
 83: 
 84:             // Re-validate the transition INSIDE the lock so the
 85:             // current status is the one we are actually transitioning
 86:             // from, not a snapshot that could be stale by now.
 87:             if (isset($data['status'])) {
 88:                 $this->transitionService->validateTransition($locked, $data['status']);
 89:             }
 90: 
 91:             $oldDetails = $locked->details()->orderBy('id')->get()->toArray();
 92: 
 93:             // Historical complaints (imported for archival) must never
 94:             // trigger a stock diff — their details were saved without
 95:             // stock deduction, so "restoring" and "re-deducting" would
 96:             // either corrupt inventory or double-count.
 97:             $hasHistoricalDetails = collect($oldDetails)->contains(
 98:                 fn ($d) => ($d['source_type'] ?? '') === 'historical'
 99:             );
100: 
101:             $processedDetails = null;
102: 
103:             if (! $hasHistoricalDetails && $detallar !== null && is_array($detallar)) {
104:                 $location = ($data['yer'] ?? null) instanceof Location
105:                     ? $data['yer']->value
106:                     : ($data['yer'] ?? 'garage');
107: 
108:                 $processedDetails = $this->stockService->syncStockDiff(
109:                     $oldDetails,
110:                     $detallar,
111:                     $location,
112:                     $data['service_vehicle_id'] ?? null,
113:                     $locked->service_vehicle_id
114:                 );
115:             }
116: 
117:             $locked->update($data);
118: 
119:             // Historical complaints keep their original details untouched.
120:             if ($processedDetails !== null) {
121:                 $this->syncDetails($locked, $processedDetails);
122:             }
123: 
124:             $this->itemService->syncItems($locked, $shikayet, $data['complaint_type'] ?? null);
125: 
126:             return $locked->fresh(['details', 'items']);
127:         });
128: 
129:         // The PDF (if any) now shows an outdated snapshot. Delete it
130:         // after the transaction commits so a rollback never removes
131:         // a still-valid file.
132:         $this->invalidatePdfAfterCommit($updated);
133: 
134:         return $updated;
135:     }
136: 
137:     public function close(Complaint $complaint, array $data): Complaint
138:     {
139:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($complaint, $data) {
140:             // ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
141:             // Lock the complaint row so two concurrent close attempts
142:             // are serialized. Without this, both could pass the
143:             // "isCompleted?" pre-check outside the transaction and
144:             // both succeed — the second one silently overwriting the
145:             // first one's end_date / end_time / closed_by values.
146:             $locked = Complaint::withoutGlobalScopes()
147:                 ->whereKey($complaint->getKey())
148:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
149:                 ->lockForUpdate()
150:                 ->firstOrFail();
151: 
152:             $this->transitionService->validateTransition(
153:                 $locked,
154:                 ComplaintStatus::Completed
155:             );
156: 
157:             $locked->update([
158:                 'status' => ComplaintStatus::Completed,
159:                 'end_date' => $data['end_date'],
160:                 'end_time' => $data['end_time'],
161:                 'work_done_by' => $data['work_done'],
162:                 'closed_at' => now(),
163:                 'closed_by' => auth()->id(),
164:             ]);
165: 
166:             return $locked;
167:         });
168:     }
169: 
170:     public function delete(Complaint $complaint): void
171:     {
172:         DB::transaction(function () use ($complaint) {
173:             // ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
174:             // Lock the complaint row so a concurrent update / close /
175:             // delete on the same row is serialized. Without this, a
176:             // delete could run in parallel with an update that has
177:             // already read the "old" details — both would restore
178:             // stock for the same rows, doubling the credited quantity.
179:             $locked = Complaint::withoutGlobalScopes()
180:                 ->whereKey($complaint->getKey())
181:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
182:                 ->lockForUpdate()
183:                 ->first();
184: 
185:             if (! $locked) {
186:                 // Already deleted by another process. Nothing to do.
187:                 return;
188:             }
189: 
190:             // Restore stock for all details. For road complaints, the
191:             // stock goes back to the specific service vehicle that was
192:             // linked to this complaint.
193:             if ($locked->details->isNotEmpty()) {
194:                 $this->stockService->restoreStock(
195:                     $locked->details->toArray(),
196:                     $locked->service_vehicle_id
197:                 );
198:             }
199: 
200:             // AUDIT NOTE
201:             // ----------
202:             // `$locked->details()->delete()` is a Builder-level bulk
203:             // delete — it bypasses Eloquent's `deleted` event, so the
204:             // Auditable trait writes NO log for the details. We take
205:             // an explicit audit snapshot first, mirroring the pattern
206:             // used by BusService::bulkDelete().
207:             //
208:             // The complaint row itself is deleted via `$locked->delete()`
209:             // (per-model), so its audit entry is written normally.
210:             $detailIds = $locked->details()->pluck('id')->all();
211: 
212:             if (! empty($detailIds)) {
213:                 ComplaintDetail::auditBulkDelete($detailIds);
214:             }
215: 
216:             // Soft-delete details
217:             $locked->details()->delete();
218: 
219:             // Soft-delete complaint
220:             $locked->delete();
221:         });
222: 
223:         $this->invalidatePdfAfterCommit($complaint);
224:     }
225: 
226:     /**
227:      * Bulk soft-delete multiple complaints.
228:      *
229:      * Each complaint is deleted through the existing delete() method
230:      * so that stock restoration, detail cascades, and per-row audit
231:      * logging all run exactly as they do for single-row deletes.
232:      *
233:      * The IDs are processed in CHUNKS, each chunk inside its own
234:      * transaction. This is a deliberate trade-off:
235:      *
236:      *   - One giant transaction over 2000+ rows holds table locks
237:      *     for too long, blocks other users, and risks PHP timeouts.
238:      *   - One transaction per row would be correct but slow.
239:      *
240:      * Chunking gives us atomicity at a reasonable granularity while
241:      * keeping each transaction short. If a chunk fails, earlier
242:      * chunks stay committed — the operator sees a partial-success
243:      * count and can retry the remainder.
244:      *
245:      * Eager-loads `details` on every chunk to avoid an N+1 query
246:      * inside delete()->restoreStock().
247:      *
248:      * @param  array<int>  $ids
249:      * @return int Number of complaints actually deleted
250:      */
251:     public function bulkDelete(array $ids, int $chunkSize = 100): int
252:     {
253:         if (empty($ids)) {
254:             return 0;
255:         }
256: 
257:         $deleted = 0;
258: 
259:         foreach (array_chunk($ids, $chunkSize) as $chunk) {
260:             DB::transaction(function () use ($chunk, &$deleted) {
261:                 $complaints = Complaint::with('details')
262:                     ->whereIn('id', $chunk)
263:                     ->get();
264: 
265:                 foreach ($complaints as $complaint) {
266:                     $this->delete($complaint);
267:                     $deleted++;
268:                 }
269:             });
270:         }
271: 
272:         return $deleted;
273:     }
274: 
275:     /**
276:      * Bulk soft-delete ALL complaints matching the given Eloquent query.
277:      *
278:      * Memory-safe: the ID stream is pulled from the database in
279:      * fixed-size chunks via chunkById().
280:      *
281:      * Chunk-level atomicity means a failure partway through leaves
282:      * earlier chunks committed. The caller receives the partial count
283:      * so it can show the operator what actually happened; the log
284:      * entry records which chunk failed.
285:      *
286:      * @param  \Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder<Complaint>  $query
287:      * @return array{deleted: int, error: ?string}
288:      */
289:     public function bulkDeleteByQuery($query, int $chunkSize = 100): array
290:     {
291:         $deleted = 0;
292:         $error = null;
293: 
294:         $idQuery = $query->clone()
295:             ->reorder()
296:             ->setEagerLoads([])
297:             ->select('complaints.id');
298: 
299:         try {
300:             $idQuery->chunkById($chunkSize, function ($rows) use (&$deleted) {
301:                 $ids = $rows->pluck('id')->all();
302: 
303:                 if (empty($ids)) {
304:                     return;
305:                 }
306: 
307:                 DB::transaction(function () use ($ids, &$deleted) {
308:                     $complaints = Complaint::with('details')
309:                         ->whereIn('id', $ids)
310:                         ->get();
311: 
312:                     foreach ($complaints as $complaint) {
313:                         $this->delete($complaint);
314:                         $deleted++;
315:                     }
316:                 });
317:             }, 'complaints.id', 'id');
318:         } catch (\Throwable $e) {
319:             // Preserve the partial count so the caller can report it.
320:             $error = $e->getMessage();
321: 
322:             Log::error('Bulk complaint delete aborted mid-run', [
323:                 'deleted_so_far' => $deleted,
324:                 'error' => $error,
325:                 'user_id' => auth()->id(),
326:                 'request_id' => Context::get('request_id'),
327:             ]);
328:         }
329: 
330:         return ['deleted' => $deleted, 'error' => $error];
331:     }
332: 
333:     /**
334:      * Register PDF invalidation to run after the enclosing transaction
335:      * commits.
336:      *
337:      * Rationale: delete() is called inside bulkDelete()'s chunk
338:      * transaction. If we deleted the PDF immediately and the chunk
339:      * later rolled back, the complaint would still exist but its PDF
340:      * would be gone — forcing a needless regeneration. DB::afterCommit()
341:      * defers the deletion until the outermost transaction commits.
342:      *
343:      * When there is no active transaction, the callback fires
344:      * immediately — which is the correct behavior for the standalone
345:      * update() / delete() paths.
346:      */
347:     protected function invalidatePdfAfterCommit(Complaint $complaint): void
348:     {
349:         DB::afterCommit(function () use ($complaint) {
350:             $this->invalidatePdf($complaint);
351:         });
352:     }
353: 
354:     /**
355:      * Best-effort removal of the stale PDF for a complaint.
356:      *
357:      * Failure is logged but never propagated: the primary operation
358:      * (update or delete) has already succeeded, and a leftover file
359:      * is strictly better than a rollback.
360:      */
361:     protected function invalidatePdf(Complaint $complaint): void
362:     {
363:         try {
364:             $this->pdfService->delete($complaint);
365:         } catch (\Throwable $e) {
366:             Log::warning('Failed to invalidate stale complaint PDF', [
367:                 'complaint_id' => $complaint->id,
368:                 'error' => $e->getMessage(),
369:                 'request_id' => Context::get('request_id'),
370:             ]);
371:         }
372:     }
373: 
374:     /**
375:      * Normalise the driver + service vehicle fields based on the location.
376:      *
377:      * Rules:
378:      *   yer = road   → driver_id required (from form), driver_name filled
379:      *                  from the driver's full name; service_vehicle_id kept
380:      *                  exactly as the operator selected it (NEVER inferred)
381:      *   yer = garage → driver + service vehicle both cleared
382:      */
383:     private function applyLocationContext(array &$data): void
384:     {
385:         $location = $data['yer'] ?? null;
386: 
387:         $isRoad = $location === Location::Road->value
388:             || ($location instanceof Location && $location->isRoad());
389: 
390:         if ($isRoad) {
391:             if (! empty($data['driver_id'])) {
392:                 $driver = Driver::active()->findOrFail($data['driver_id']);
393:                 $data['driver_name'] = $driver->full_name;
394:             }
395: 
396:             return;
397:         }
398: 
399:         // Garage complaints have no driver and no service vehicle.
400:         $data['driver_id'] = null;
401:         $data['driver_name'] = null;
402:         $data['service_vehicle_id'] = null;
403:     }
404: 
405:     /**
406:      * In-place sync of complaint details.
407:      *
408:      * Rows are matched by their `code` value and updated in place (IDs preserved).
409:      * New codes are inserted, removed codes are soft-deleted.
410:      *
411:      * @param  array<int, array<string, mixed>>  $processedDetails
412:      */
413:     private function syncDetails(Complaint $complaint, array $processedDetails): void
414:     {
415:         // ==================== 0. PREPARE ====================
416:         // NOTE: this method keys details by their `code` value. If two
417:         // rows in $processedDetails share a code, the later one silently
418:         // overwrites the earlier. FormRequests reject this at the input
419:         // layer (see ComplaintStoreRequest/ComplaintUpdateRequest
420:         // withValidator), so this is a defense-in-depth assertion only.
421:         $existingByCode = $complaint->details()
422:             ->orderBy('id')
423:             ->get()
424:             ->keyBy('code');
425: 
426:         $newByCode = [];
427:         foreach ($processedDetails as $detail) {
428:             $code = $detail['code'] ?? null;
429:             if ($code !== null && $code !== '') {
430:                 $newByCode[$code] = $detail;
431:             }
432:         }
433: 
434:         $existingCodes = $existingByCode->keys()->all();
435:         $newCodes = array_keys($newByCode);
436: 
437:         // ==================== 1. UPDATE EXISTING ====================
438:         $codesToUpdate = array_intersect($existingCodes, $newCodes);
439:         foreach ($codesToUpdate as $code) {
440:             /** @var ComplaintDetail $detail */
441:             $detail = $existingByCode[$code];
442:             $payload = $newByCode[$code];
443: 
444:             $detail->update($payload);
445:         }
446: 
447:         // ==================== 2. CREATE NEW ====================
448:         $codesToCreate = array_diff($newCodes, $existingCodes);
449:         $payloadsToCreate = [];
450:         foreach ($codesToCreate as $code) {
451:             $payloadsToCreate[] = $newByCode[$code];
452:         }
453:         if (! empty($payloadsToCreate)) {
454:             $complaint->details()->createMany($payloadsToCreate);
455:         }
456: 
457:         // ==================== 3. SOFT-DELETE REMOVED ====================
458:         $codesToDelete = array_diff($existingCodes, $newCodes);
459:         foreach ($codesToDelete as $code) {
460:             /** @var ComplaintDetail $detail */
461:             $detail = $existingByCode[$code];
462:             $detail->delete();
463:         }
464:     }
465: }
</file>

<file path="app/Services/Complaint/ComplaintStatusTransitionService.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services\Complaint;
 4: 
 5: use App\Enums\ComplaintStatus;
 6: use App\Models\Complaint;
 7: use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
 8: 
 9: class ComplaintStatusTransitionService
10: {
11:     /**
12:      * Validate that the requested status change is legal.
13:      *
14:      * `$complaint->status` is now cast to ComplaintStatus via the
15:      * model, so we can read it directly. If the DB value is unknown
16:      * (should not happen — enforced by a CHECK constraint), we fall
17:      * back to Pending.
18:      */
19:     public function validateTransition(Complaint $complaint, string|ComplaintStatus $newStatus): void
20:     {
21:         $current = $complaint->status instanceof ComplaintStatus
22:             ? $complaint->status
23:             : ComplaintStatus::Pending;
24: 
25:         $next = $newStatus instanceof ComplaintStatus
26:             ? $newStatus
27:             : ComplaintStatus::tryFrom($newStatus);
28: 
29:         if ($next === null) {
30:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
31:                 'status' => __('messages.flash.invalid_status_transition', [
32:                     'from' => $current->value,
33:                     'to' => (string) $newStatus,
34:                 ]),
35:             ]);
36:         }
37: 
38:         if ($current === $next) {
39:             return;
40:         }
41: 
42:         if (! $current->canTransitionTo($next)) {
43:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
44:                 'status' => __('messages.flash.invalid_status_transition', [
45:                     'from' => $current->value,
46:                     'to' => $next->value,
47:                 ]),
48:             ]);
49:         }
50:     }
51: }

<file path="app/Services/Complaint/ComplaintStockService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\Complaint;
  4: 
  5: use App\Exceptions\MissingGarageContextException;
  6: use App\Models\ServiceVehicle;
  7: use App\Models\ServiceVehicleStock;
  8: use App\Models\Warehouse;
  9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
 10: use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
 11: 
 12: /**
 13:  * Handles stock changes caused by complaint details.
 14:  *
 15:  * ── SOURCE SELECTION ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 16:  * The location of the complaint (`yer`) determines the source of parts:
 17:  *
 18:  *   yer = 'garage' → the source garage's own warehouse
 19:  *   yer = 'road'   → the SPECIFIC service vehicle selected on the
 20:  *                    complaint (service_vehicle_id)
 21:  *
 22:  * There is NO fallback. If the selected vehicle does not have enough
 23:  * stock, the complaint write is rejected. Filling the service vehicle
 24:  * is the warehouse officer's job — the complaint operator must not
 25:  * silently pull from the warehouse instead.
 26:  *
 27:  * Legacy road complaints created before the service_vehicle_id column
 28:  * existed have a NULL vehicle. Their stock cannot be restored
 29:  * automatically on delete; this is logged at warning level rather than
 30:  * silently dropped.
 31:  */
 32: class ComplaintStockService
 33: {
 34:     /**
 35:      * Fail-closed guard for every stock mutation in this service.
 36:      *
 37:      * The queries below use withoutGlobalScopes() so that the service
 38:      * also works in queue jobs and console commands (where the
 39:      * HasGarageScope global scope may be inactive). That escape hatch
 40:      * has a cost: if no garage is in context, the query matches rows
 41:      * from ANY tenant. On a stock mutation that is never acceptable —
 42:      * a code collision (e.g. "FILTER-001" exists in two garages) would
 43:      * silently deduct from the wrong tenant's warehouse.
 44:      *
 45:      * This guard closes the gap: any call to deductStock() or
 46:      * restoreStock() without an active garage context is rejected
 47:      * outright, regardless of environment. Console commands that
 48:      * legitimately need this service must call GarageContext::set()
 49:      * first — see DemoDataSeeder for the pattern.
 50:      *
 51:      * @throws MissingGarageContextException
 52:      */
 53:     private function requireGarageId(): int
 54:     {
 55:         $garageId = \App\Services\GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
 56: 
 57:         if ($garageId === null || $garageId <= 0) {
 58:             throw new MissingGarageContextException(
 59:                 static::class,
 60:                 sprintf(
 61:                     '%s requires an active garage context. '
 62:                     .'Call GarageContext::set($garageId, $companyId) '
 63:                     .'before invoking deductStock() / restoreStock().',
 64:                     static::class,
 65:                 ),
 66:             );
 67:         }
 68: 
 69:         return (int) $garageId;
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     /**
 73:      * Deduct stock for the given detail payloads.
 74:      *
 75:      * @param  array<int, array<string, mixed>>  $details
 76:      * @param  string  $location  'road' | 'garage'
 77:      * @param  int|null  $serviceVehicleId  Required when $location === 'road'
 78:      * @return array<int, array<string, mixed>> Only rows that actually affect stock
 79:      */
 80:     public function deductStock(
 81:         array $details,
 82:         string $location = 'garage',
 83:         ?int $serviceVehicleId = null
 84:     ): array {
 85:         // Fail-closed: never mutate stock without a known garage.
 86:         $this->requireGarageId();
 87: 
 88:         // ── DEADLOCK GUARD: deterministic lock order ──
 89:         //
 90:         // Both this method and restoreStock() acquire row-level locks
 91:         // (lockForUpdate) on warehouse / service-vehicle rows. If two
 92:         // concurrent transactions touch the SAME set of codes in
 93:         // different orders — e.g. one user reordered the parts while
 94:         // another user updated the complaint — PostgreSQL detects a
 95:         // cycle and aborts one of them with a deadlock error.
 96:         //
 97:         // Sorting the input by `code` guarantees that every
 98:         // transaction acquires locks in the same alphabetical order,
 99:         // regardless of the order the operator entered the rows.
100:         //
101:         // The output array ($processed) is built in sorted order,
102:         // which is safe because:
103:         //   - each code is unique (FormRequest rejects duplicates),
104:         //   - ComplaintService::syncDetails() keys by code,
105:         //   - restoreStock() already uses the same sort order, so
106:         //     the diff walks the rows on both sides identically.
107:         $sorted = collect($details)
108:             ->sortBy(fn ($detail) => (string) ($detail['code'] ?? ''))
109:             ->values()
110:             ->all();
111: 
112:         $processed = [];
113: 
114:         foreach ($sorted as $detail) {
115:             $code = $detail['code'] ?? null;
116: 
117:             if (empty($code)) {
118:                 continue;
119:             }
120: 
121:             $usedQuantity = (int) ($detail['used_quantity'] ?? 0);
122: 
123:             // ── Inspection / repair-only row ──
124:             if ($usedQuantity <= 0) {
125:                 $processed[] = [
126:                     'shikayet_index' => $detail['shikayet_index'] ?? 0,
127:                     'code' => $code,
128:                     'name' => $detail['name'] ?? $code,
129:                     'stock_quantity' => 0,
130:                     'used_quantity' => 0,
131:                     'price_at_use' => 0,
132:                     'employee_id' => $detail['employee_id'] ?? null,
133:                     'notes' => $detail['notes'] ?? null,
134:                     'source_type' => 'inspection',
135:                 ];
136: 
137:                 continue;
138:             }
139: 
140:             // ── Existing logic for consumed parts ──
141:             if ($location === 'road') {
142:                 $processed[] = $this->deductFromServiceVehicle(
143:                     $detail, $code, $usedQuantity, $serviceVehicleId
144:                 );
145: 
146:                 continue;
147:             }
148: 
149:             $processed[] = $this->deductFromWarehouse($detail, $code, $usedQuantity);
150:         }
151: 
152:         return $processed;
153:     }
154: 
155:     /**
156:      * Restore stock for the given details (used on complaint delete
157:      * or when replacing details during an update).
158:      *
159:      * The `source_type` recorded on each detail decides where the
160:      * stock goes back to. For `service_vehicle` rows, the caller must
161:      * pass the complaint's `service_vehicle_id`.
162:      *
163:      * DEADLOCK GUARD: rows are sorted by `code` before any lock is
164:      * acquired. Two concurrent deletes that touch the same warehouse
165:      * rows in a different order would otherwise deadlock on
166:      * PostgreSQL's row-level locks (transaction A locks W-001 then
167:      * W-002, transaction B locks W-002 then W-001, both wait forever).
168:      * Sorting makes every transaction acquire locks in the same
169:      * order, eliminating the cycle.
170:      *
171:      * @param  array<int, array<string, mixed>>  $details
172:      * @param  int|null  $serviceVehicleId  Vehicle to credit when restoring
173:      */
174:     public function restoreStock(array $details, ?int $serviceVehicleId = null): void
175:     {
176:         // Fail-closed: never mutate stock without a known garage.
177:         $garageId = $this->requireGarageId();
178: 
179:         // ── Deterministic lock order ──
180:         // Filter out rows that will never touch stock, then sort by
181:         // code so both warehouse and vehicle branches see a stable
182:         // sequence.
183:         $sortedDetails = collect($details)
184:             ->filter(function ($detail) {
185:                 $code = $detail['code'] ?? null;
186:                 $qty = (int) ($detail['used_quantity'] ?? 0);
187: 
188:                 return ! empty($code) && $qty > 0;
189:             })
190:             ->sortBy('code')
191:             ->values()
192:             ->all();
193: 
194:         foreach ($sortedDetails as $detail) {
195:             $code = $detail['code'];
196:             $usedQuantity = (int) $detail['used_quantity'];
197:             $sourceType = $detail['source_type'] ?? 'warehouse';
198: 
199:             // Historical imports and inspection rows never touched
200:             // stock on creation, so there is nothing to restore.
201:             if (in_array($sourceType, ['historical', 'inspection'], true)) {
202:                 continue;
203:             }
204: 
205:             // ── Service vehicle: restore to the specific vehicle ──
206:             if ($sourceType === 'service_vehicle') {
207:                 if ($serviceVehicleId === null) {
208:                     // Legacy road complaint created before the
209:                     // service_vehicle_id column existed — cannot
210:                     // restore automatically. Log and skip.
211:                     Log::warning('Service vehicle id missing — stock restore skipped', [
212:                         'code' => $code,
213:                         'quantity' => $usedQuantity,
214:                     ]);
215: 
216:                     continue;
217:                 }
218: 
219:                 $this->restoreToSpecificVehicle(
220:                     $code,
221:                     $usedQuantity,
222:                     $serviceVehicleId,
223:                     $detail['name'] ?? null
224:                 );
225: 
226:                 continue;
227:             }
228: 
229:             // ── Warehouse: restore to the garage warehouse ──
230:             //
231:             // The garage filter is mandatory (not conditional) — the
232:             // guard at the top of this method already established that
233:             // a garage is in context, so we lock the row inside that
234:             // garage only. Quarantine rows are excluded: crediting a
235:             // restored quantity to a quarantine bucket would silently
236:             // "clean" defective stock and corrupt the active inventory
237:             // balance.
238:             $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
239:                 ->where('code', $code)
240:                 ->where('is_quarantine', false)
241:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
242:                 ->where('garage_id', $garageId)
243:                 ->lockForUpdate()
244:                 ->first();
245: 
246:             if ($warehouse) {
247:                 $warehouse->increment('quantity', $usedQuantity);
248: 
249:                 continue;
250:             }
251: 
252:             // Warehouse row not found — this should not happen if the
253:             // original deduction succeeded, but log it for safety.
254:             Log::warning('Warehouse row not found — stock restore skipped', [
255:                 'code' => $code,
256:                 'quantity' => $usedQuantity,
257:                 'garage_id' => $garageId,
258:             ]);
259:         }
260:     }
261: 
262:     /**
263:      * Reconcile stock after an edit: restore old usage and deduct new usage.
264:      *
265:      * @param  array<int, array<string, mixed>>  $oldDetails
266:      * @param  array<int, array<string, mixed>>  $newDetails
267:      */
268:     public function syncStockDiff(
269:         array $oldDetails,
270:         array $newDetails,
271:         string $location = 'garage',
272:         ?int $newServiceVehicleId = null,
273:         ?int $oldServiceVehicleId = null
274:     ): array {
275:         // Step 1: restore everything the OLD details had taken.
276:         // The old details belong to the old complaint state — in practice
277:         // the vehicle is the same, but we accept both to be safe.
278:         $this->restoreStock($oldDetails, $oldServiceVehicleId ?? $newServiceVehicleId);
279: 
280:         // Step 2: deduct the NEW details from scratch.
281:         return $this->deductStock($newDetails, $location, $newServiceVehicleId);
282:     }
283: 
284:     // ==================== PRIVATE HELPERS ====================
285: 
286:     /**
287:      * Deduct from the garage warehouse. Throws if insufficient.
288:      *
289:      * ✅ SECURITY (defense-in-depth): the query filters by the current
290:      * garage explicitly, even though HasGarageScope would normally do
291:      * it. This keeps the deduction correct when the service is invoked
292:      * from a queue job, artisan command, or an import where the global
293:      * scope may be inactive.
294:      *
295:      * Quarantine rows (is_quarantine = true) are excluded: defective
296:      * parts must never enter the active ledger through a complaint.
297:      */
298:     private function deductFromWarehouse(array $detail, string $code, int $usedQuantity): array
299:     {
300:         // Fail-closed: the guard is repeated here (in addition to the
301:         // one at the top of deductStock()) so that this method stays
302:         // safe even if it is ever called directly from a future code
303:         // path that skips the public entry point.
304:         $garageId = $this->requireGarageId();
305: 
306:         $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
307:             ->where('code', $code)
308:             ->where('is_quarantine', false)
309:             ->where('garage_id', $garageId)
310:             ->lockForUpdate()
311:             ->first();
312: 
313:         if (! $warehouse) {
314:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
315:                 'details' => __('messages.flash.stock_item_not_found', ['code' => $code]),
316:             ]);
317:         }
318: 
319:         if ($warehouse->quantity < $usedQuantity) {
320:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
321:                 'details' => __('messages.flash.stock_insufficient', [
322:                     'name' => $warehouse->name,
323:                     'requested' => $usedQuantity,
324:                     'available' => $warehouse->quantity,
325:                 ]),
326:             ]);
327:         }
328: 
329:         $row = $this->buildProcessedRow(
330:             $detail,
331:             $code,
332:             $usedQuantity,
333:             'warehouse',
334:             $warehouse,
335:             null
336:         );
337: 
338:         $warehouse->quantity -= $usedQuantity;
339:         $warehouse->save();
340: 
341:         return $row;
342:     }
343: 
344:     /**
345:      * Deduct from the SPECIFIC service vehicle selected on the complaint.
346:      * Throws if the vehicle is not provided, not found, not in the
347:      * current garage, or has insufficient stock.
348:      *
349:      * ✅ SECURITY (defense-in-depth): the vehicle must belong to the
350:      * current garage context. The FormRequest already validates this,
351:      * but a future controller, queue job, or console command might
352:      * bypass the request layer. Re-checking here closes that gap.
353:      */
354:     private function deductFromServiceVehicle(
355:         array $detail,
356:         string $code,
357:         int $usedQuantity,
358:         ?int $serviceVehicleId
359:     ): array {
360:         if ($serviceVehicleId === null) {
361:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
362:                 'service_vehicle_id' => __('messages.flash.service_vehicle_required'),
363:             ]);
364:         }
365: 
366:         // Fail-closed: the vehicle MUST belong to the current garage.
367:         $currentGarageId = $this->requireGarageId();
368: 
369:         $vehicle = ServiceVehicle::withoutGlobalScopes()
370:             ->whereKey($serviceVehicleId)
371:             ->where('garage_id', $currentGarageId)
372:             ->first();
373: 
374:         if (! $vehicle) {
375:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
376:                 'service_vehicle_id' => __('messages.flash.service_vehicle_not_found'),
377:             ]);
378:         }
379: 
380:         $stock = ServiceVehicleStock::withoutGlobalScopes()
381:             ->where('service_vehicle_id', $serviceVehicleId)
382:             ->where('code', $code)
383:             ->lockForUpdate()
384:             ->first();
385: 
386:         if (! $stock) {
387:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
388:                 'details' => __('messages.flash.service_vehicle_part_not_found', [
389:                     'code' => $code,
390:                     'vehicle' => $vehicle->name,
391:                 ]),
392:             ]);
393:         }
394: 
395:         if ($stock->quantity < $usedQuantity) {
396:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
397:                 'details' => __('messages.flash.service_vehicle_stock_insufficient', [
398:                     'name' => $stock->name,
399:                     'vehicle' => $vehicle->name,
400:                     'requested' => $usedQuantity,
401:                     'available' => $stock->quantity,
402:                 ]),
403:             ]);
404:         }
405: 
406:         $row = $this->buildProcessedRow(
407:             $detail,
408:             $code,
409:             $usedQuantity,
410:             'service_vehicle',
411:             null,
412:             $stock
413:         );
414: 
415:         $stock->decrement('quantity', $usedQuantity);
416: 
417:         return $row;
418:     }
419: 
420:     /**
421:      * Give stock back to the specific service vehicle.
422:      *
423:      * If the vehicle no longer has a stock row for this code (e.g. it
424:      * was fully depleted and cleaned up), the row is re-created from
425:      * the detail's metadata so the quantity is never silently lost.
426:      */
427:     private function restoreToSpecificVehicle(
428:         string $code,
429:         int $quantity,
430:         int $serviceVehicleId,
431:         ?string $nameFromDetail = null
432:     ): void {
433:         // Fail-closed: only restore to a vehicle that belongs to the
434:         // current garage. A stale complaint referencing a foreign
435:         // vehicle must never silently credit a foreign tenant.
436:         $currentGarageId = $this->requireGarageId();
437: 
438:         $vehicle = ServiceVehicle::withoutGlobalScopes()
439:             ->whereKey($serviceVehicleId)
440:             ->where('garage_id', $currentGarageId)
441:             ->first();
442:         if (! $vehicle) {
443:             Log::warning('Service vehicle not found — stock restore skipped', [
444:                 'service_vehicle_id' => $serviceVehicleId,
445:                 'code' => $code,
446:                 'quantity' => $quantity,
447:             ]);
448: 
449:             return;
450:         }
451: 
452:         $stock = ServiceVehicleStock::withoutGlobalScopes()
453:             ->where('service_vehicle_id', $serviceVehicleId)
454:             ->where('code', $code)
455:             ->lockForUpdate()
456:             ->first();
457: 
458:         if ($stock) {
459:             $stock->increment('quantity', $quantity);
460: 
461:             return;
462:         }
463: 
464:         // Recreate the row. Fall back to the warehouse row for a
465:         // canonical name/unit when the detail carried no name.
466:         $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
467:             ->where('garage_id', $vehicle->garage_id)
468:             ->where('code', $code)
469:             ->where('is_quarantine', false)
470:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
471:             ->first();
472: 
473:         ServiceVehicleStock::withoutGlobalScopes()->create([
474:             'service_vehicle_id' => $serviceVehicleId,
475:             'garage_id' => $vehicle->garage_id,
476:             'company_id' => $vehicle->company_id,
477:             'code' => $code,
478:             'name' => $warehouse->name ?? $nameFromDetail ?? $code,
479:             'unit' => $warehouse->unit ?? null,
480:             'quantity' => $quantity,
481:         ]);
482:     }
483: 
484:     /**
485:      * Build the row that will be persisted on complaint_details.
486:      */
487:     private function buildProcessedRow(
488:         array $detail,
489:         string $code,
490:         int $usedQuantity,
491:         string $sourceType,
492:         ?Warehouse $warehouse = null,
493:         ?ServiceVehicleStock $stock = null
494:     ): array {
495:         $name = $warehouse?->name ?? $stock?->name ?? $code;
496: 
497:         // Price snapshot — see migration 2026_09_18_120000
498:         $priceAtUse = $this->resolvePrice($warehouse, $stock, $code);
499: 
500:         return [
501:             'shikayet_index' => $detail['shikayet_index'] ?? 0,
502:             'code' => $code,
503:             'name' => $name,
504:             'stock_quantity' => $sourceType === 'warehouse'
505:                 ? ($warehouse?->quantity ?? 0)
506:                 : ($stock?->quantity ?? 0),
507:             'used_quantity' => $usedQuantity,
508:             'price_at_use' => $priceAtUse,
509:             'employee_id' => $detail['employee_id'] ?? null,
510:             'notes' => $detail['notes'] ?? null,
511:             'source_type' => $sourceType,
512:         ];
513:     }
514: 
515:     /**
516:      * Resolve the unit price to snapshot for this detail row.
517:      *
518:      *   - warehouse source     → warehouse.price
519:      *   - service vehicle      → warehouse.price for the same code in the
520:      *                            same garage (vehicle stocks have no price)
521:      *   - unknown              → null
522:      */
523:     private function resolvePrice(
524:         ?Warehouse $warehouse,
525:         ?ServiceVehicleStock $stock,
526:         string $code
527:     ): ?float {
528:         if ($warehouse !== null) {
529:             return $warehouse->price !== null ? (float) $warehouse->price : null;
530:         }
531: 
532:         if ($stock !== null) {
533:             $fallback = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
534:                 ->where('garage_id', $stock->garage_id)
535:                 ->where('code', $code)
536:                 ->where('is_quarantine', false)
537:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
538:                 ->value('price');
539: 
540:             return $fallback !== null ? (float) $fallback : null;
541:         }
542: 
543:         return null;
544:     }
545: }

<file path="app/Services/GarageContext.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\Garage;
  6: use App\Models\User;
  7: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
  8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context;
  9: 
 10: /**
 11:  * Centralized accessor for the "current garage" and "current company"
 12:  * of the active request.
 13:  *
 14:  * Resolution order (first hit wins):
 15:  *   1. Laravel Context      — set by middleware, most reliable
 16:  *   2. Session              — set at login / garage selection
 17:  *   3. Authenticated user   — persisted preference; needed for queue
 18:  *                             jobs and console contexts
 19:  *   4. null                 — no context available
 20:  *
 21:  * Two read APIs:
 22:  *   - getGarageId() / getCompanyId(): raw Context only. Use when the
 23:  *     caller is guaranteed to run behind the garage.selected middleware.
 24:  *   - resolveGarageId() / resolveCompanyId(): full fallback chain. Use
 25:  *     in services, models, and background jobs.
 26:  */
 27: class GarageContext
 28: {
 29:     // ==================== WRITE ====================
 30: 
 31:     public static function set(int $garageId, ?int $companyId = null): void
 32:     {
 33:         Context::add('current_garage_id', $garageId);
 34:         Context::add('current_company_id', $companyId);
 35:     }
 36: 
 37:     /**
 38:      * Populate Context from a User's persisted current_garage_id.
 39:      *
 40:      * Returns true when the Context was set. The garage is verified
 41:      * to exist and to be active; a user whose persisted garage has
 42:      * since been soft-deleted or deactivated is treated as having no
 43:      * context, so downstream queries fall back to the standard
 44:      * "missing context" path instead of operating on a dead tenant.
 45:      */
 46:     public static function fromUser(User $user): bool
 47:     {
 48:         if (! $user->current_garage_id) {
 49:             return false;
 50:         }
 51: 
 52:         $garage = Garage::withoutGlobalScopes()
 53:             ->whereKey($user->current_garage_id)
 54:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 55:             ->where('is_active', true)
 56:             ->first();
 57: 
 58:         if (! $garage) {
 59:             return false;
 60:         }
 61: 
 62:         self::set(
 63:             (int) $garage->id,
 64:             $garage->company_id ? (int) $garage->company_id : null,
 65:         );
 66: 
 67:         return true;
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     public static function clear(): void
 71:     {
 72:         Context::forget('current_garage_id');
 73:         Context::forget('current_company_id');
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     // ==================== READ (raw Context) ====================
 77: 
 78:     /**
 79:      * Raw Context value — no fallback. Use only when the caller is
 80:      * guaranteed to run behind `garage.selected`.
 81:      */
 82:     public static function getGarageId(): ?int
 83:     {
 84:         return Context::get('current_garage_id');
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     public static function getCompanyId(): ?int
 88:     {
 89:         return Context::get('current_company_id');
 90:     }
 91: 
 92:     public static function has(): bool
 93:     {
 94:         return Context::has('current_garage_id');
 95:     }
 96: 
 97:     // ==================== READ (resolved with fallback) ====================
 98: 
 99:     /**
100:      * Resolve the current garage id, walking the full fallback chain.
101:      */
102:     public static function resolveGarageId(): ?int
103:     {
104:         return self::getGarageId()
105:             ?? self::fromSession('current_garage_id')
106:             ?? self::fromAuth('current_garage_id');
107:     }
108: 
109:     /**
110:      * Resolve the current company id, walking the full fallback chain.
111:      */
112:     public static function resolveCompanyId(): ?int
113:     {
114:         return self::getCompanyId()
115:             ?? self::fromSession('current_company_id')
116:             ?? self::fromAuth('current_company_id');
117:     }
118: 
119:     /**
120:      * Resolve the full Garage model, if the resolved id points to an
121:      * existing record.
122:      */
123:     public static function resolveGarage(): ?Garage
124:     {
125:         $id = self::resolveGarageId();
126: 
127:         return $id ? Garage::withoutGlobalScopes()->find($id) : null;
128:     }
129: 
130:     // ==================== FALLBACK HELPERS ====================
131: 
132:     private static function fromSession(string $key): ?int
133:     {
134:         try {
135:             $value = session($key);
136: 
137:             return $value !== null ? (int) $value : null;
138:         } catch (\Throwable $e) {
139:             return null;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     private static function fromAuth(string $key): ?int
144:     {
145:         try {
146:             $user = Auth::user();
147: 
148:             if (! $user) {
149:                 return null;
150:             }
151: 
152:             $value = $user->{$key} ?? null;
153: 
154:             return $value !== null ? (int) $value : null;
155:         } catch (\Throwable $e) {
156:             return null;
157:         }
158:     }
159: }
</file>

<file path="app/Services/OilChange/OilChangeService.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services\OilChange;
 4: 
 5: use App\Enums\OilType;
 6: use App\Models\Bus;
 7: use App\Models\BusOilChange;
 8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 9: 
10: class OilChangeService
11: {
12:     /**
13:      * Create a new oil change record.
14:      *
15:      * The interval is snapshotted from config at the moment of creation
16:      * so historical reports stay stable even if config changes later.
17:      */
18:     public function create(Bus $bus, array $data): BusOilChange
19:     {
20:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($bus, $data) {
21:             $type = OilType::from($data['oil_type']);
22:             $brand = $type->usesBrand() ? ($data['oil_brand'] ?? null) : null;
23:             $actual = (int) $data['actual_km'];
24: 
25:             $interval = $this->resolveInterval($bus, $type, $brand);
26: 
27:             return BusOilChange::create([
28:                 'bus_id' => $bus->id,
29:                 'oil_type' => $type->value,
30:                 'oil_brand' => $brand,
31:                 'scheduled_km' => $data['scheduled_km'] ?? null,
32:                 'actual_km' => $actual,
33:                 'interval_km' => $interval,
34:                 'changed_at' => $data['changed_at'] ?? null,
35:                 'notes' => $data['notes'] ?? null,
36:             ]);
37:         });
38:     }
39: 
40:     public function update(BusOilChange $change, array $data): BusOilChange
41:     {
42:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($change, $data) {
43:             $type = OilType::from($data['oil_type'] ?? $change->oil_type->value);
44:             $brand = $type->usesBrand()
45:                 ? ($data['oil_brand'] ?? $change->oil_brand)
46:                 : null;
47: 
48:             $typeChanged = $type->value !== $change->oil_type->value;
49:             $brandChanged = $brand !== $change->oil_brand;
50:             $shouldRecalculate = $typeChanged || $brandChanged;
51: 
52:             $interval = $shouldRecalculate
53:                 ? $this->resolveInterval($change->bus, $type, $brand)
54:                 : $change->interval_km;
55: 
56:             $change->update([
57:                 'oil_type' => $type->value,
58:                 'oil_brand' => $brand,
59:                 'scheduled_km' => $data['scheduled_km'] ?? $change->scheduled_km,
60:                 'actual_km' => (int) ($data['actual_km'] ?? $change->actual_km),
61:                 'interval_km' => $interval,
62:                 'changed_at' => $data['changed_at'] ?? $change->changed_at,
63:                 'notes' => $data['notes'] ?? $change->notes,
64:             ]);
65: 
66:             return $change->fresh();
67:         });
68:     }
69: 
70:     public function delete(BusOilChange $change): void
71:     {
72:         $change->delete();
73:     }
74: 
75:     /**
76:      * The interval to record for a specific change.
77:      */
78:     private function resolveInterval(Bus $bus, OilType $type, ?string $brand): int
79:     {
80:         return match ($type) {
81:             OilType::Motor => $bus->motorOilIntervalKm(),
82:             OilType::Axle => $bus->axleOilIntervalKm(),
83:             OilType::Gearbox => Bus::gearboxIntervalForBrand($brand),
84:         };
85:     }
86: }

45:             default => 'secondary',
46:         };
47:     }

<file path="app/Services/OilChange/OilChangeStatusService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\OilChange;
  4: 
  5: use App\Enums\OilType;
  6: use App\Models\Bus;
  7: use App\Models\BusOilChange;
  8: use App\Models\MotorOilDetail;
  9: 
 10: class OilChangeStatusService
 11: {
 12:     /**
 13:      * Per-request cache of catalog milestones, keyed by brand_id.
 14:      * Avoids N+1 queries when rendering a long list of buses.
 15:      *
 16:      * @var array<string, array<int>>
 17:      */
 18:     private array $catalogCache = [];
 19: 
 20:     public function forBus(Bus $bus, OilType $type): OilChangeStatus
 21:     {
 22:         $last = $this->resolveLastChange($bus, $type);
 23: 
 24:         $currentKm = (int) (
 25:             $bus->relationLoaded('latestKmRecord')
 26:                 ? ($bus->latestKmRecord?->km ?? $bus->km)
 27:                 : ($bus->latestKmRecord()->value('km') ?? $bus->km)
 28:         ) ?? 0;
 29: 
 30:         if (! $last) {
 31:             return new OilChangeStatus(
 32:                 bus: $bus,
 33:                 type: $type,
 34:                 lastChange: null,
 35:                 currentKm: $currentKm,
 36:                 nextDueKm: null,
 37:                 remainingKm: null,
 38:                 status: 'no-history',
 39:                 nextCatalogKm: null,
 40:             );
 41:         }
 42: 
 43:         // Interval selection.
 44:         //
 45:         // The `interval_km` column on BusOilChange is a SNAPSHOT of
 46:         // the interval that applied when the change was recorded —
 47:         // see OilChangeService::resolveInterval(), which reads the
 48:         // config-driven values at creation time.
 49:         //
 50:         // Gearbox intervals are brand-dependent (SHELL 180,000 km,
 51:         // LUK 120,000 km — see config/oil.intervals.gearbox). The
 52:         // previous implementation hardcoded 180,000 for every gearbox
 53:         // change, ignoring the snapshot. On a LUK-equipped bus the
 54:         // computed next_due was 60,000 km too far, so an overdue
 55:         // gearbox change showed as "OK" on the dashboard and the
 56:         // index page.
 57:         //
 58:         // Reading the snapshot for every oil type keeps the
 59:         // calculation consistent with OilChangeService (manual
 60:         // creation) and BusOilChange::effectiveIntervalFor()
 61:         // (median-of-history fallback), and it preserves historical
 62:         // accuracy if the config is tuned later.
 63:         $interval = $last->interval_km;
 64: 
 65:         $nextDueKm = $last->actual_km + $interval;
 66:         $remainingKm = $nextDueKm - $currentKm;
 67: 
 68:         // For motor oil, look up the next service milestone in the
 69:         // catalog (motor_oil_details). The mathematically computed
 70:         // next_due may not exist in the catalog because the catalog
 71:         // is keyed by 36,000-based service blocks, while an 18m bus
 72:         // uses a 30,000 km interval. The operator needs to see the
 73:         // catalog milestone because that is the one tied to a parts
 74:         // list.
 75:         $nextCatalogKm = $type === OilType::Motor
 76:             ? $this->nextCatalogMilestone($bus, $nextDueKm)
 77:             : null;
 78: 
 79:         return new OilChangeStatus(
 80:             bus: $bus,
 81:             type: $type,
 82:             lastChange: $last,
 83:             currentKm: $currentKm,
 84:             nextDueKm: $nextDueKm,
 85:             remainingKm: $remainingKm,
 86:             status: $this->classify($remainingKm),
 87:             nextCatalogKm: $nextCatalogKm,
 88:         );
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /**
 92:      * Resolve the most recent oil change for the given (bus, type) pair.
 93:      *
 94:      * Resolution priority — the goal is to avoid triggering a new DB
 95:      * query when the caller has already eager-loaded the data:
 96:      *
 97:      *   1. Dedicated eager-loadable relation
 98:      *      (latestMotorOilChange / latestGearboxOilChange /
 99:      *      latestAxleOilChange). These three relations together cost
100:      *      three queries for the ENTIRE bus list, regardless of how
101:      *      many buses or history rows exist. This is the preferred
102:      *      path used by DashboardController and
103:      *      OilChangeController::buildStatusRows().
104:      *
105:      *   2. Full `oilChanges` relation — legacy path. Any caller that
106:      *      still eager-loads the entire history (e.g. the show page
107:      *      for a single bus) continues to work. Kept for backward
108:      *      compatibility.
109:      *
110:      *   3. Per-bus query — last resort when nothing is loaded. This
111:      *      is the N+1 path; callers on list pages should avoid it.
112:      *
113:      * All three paths share the same underlying ordering
114:      * (`latestOfMany('actual_km')` or `sortByDesc('actual_km')`), so
115:      * the returned model is identical regardless of which branch
116:      * executes.
117:      */
118:     private function resolveLastChange(Bus $bus, OilType $type): ?BusOilChange
119:     {
120:         $relation = match ($type) {
121:             OilType::Motor => 'latestMotorOilChange',
122:             OilType::Gearbox => 'latestGearboxOilChange',
123:             OilType::Axle => 'latestAxleOilChange',
124:         };
125: 
126:         if ($bus->relationLoaded($relation)) {
127:             return $bus->getRelation($relation);
128:         }
129: 
130:         if ($bus->relationLoaded('oilChanges')) {
131:             return $bus->oilChanges
132:                 ->where('oil_type', $type)
133:                 ->sortByDesc('actual_km')
134:                 ->first();
135:         }
136: 
137:         return $bus->latestOilChange($type)->first();
138:     }
139: 
140:     /**
141:      * The next motor-oil catalog milestone for the given bus's brand,
142:      * at or after the target km.
143:      *
144:      * Falls back to the union of ALL catalog entries for the garage
145:      * when the bus has no brand assigned, so the operator still sees
146:      * a useful milestone instead of an empty column.
147:      *
148:      * Example: bus is 18m, interval = 30,000, next_due = 390,000.
149:      * The catalog (36,000-based) has ..., 360,000, 396,000, 432,000, ...
150:      * → returns 396,000 because it is the first catalog entry >= 390,000.
151:      */
152:     private function nextCatalogMilestone(Bus $bus, int $targetKm): ?int
153:     {
154:         // Cache key includes the brand so different buses with the
155:         // same brand share one query per request.
156:         $brandKey = (string) ($bus->brand_id ?? 'all');
157: 
158:         if (! array_key_exists($brandKey, $this->catalogCache)) {
159:             $query = MotorOilDetail::withoutGlobalScopes()
160:                 ->where('garage_id', $bus->garage_id);
161: 
162:             // Only narrow by brand when the bus actually has one.
163:             // Without this guard, a bus with brand_id = NULL would
164:             // filter on `whereNull('brand_id')` and get zero rows,
165:             // because every imported catalog row carries a brand.
166:             if ($bus->brand_id !== null) {
167:                 $query->where('brand_id', $bus->brand_id);
168:             }
169: 
170:             $this->catalogCache[$brandKey] = $query
171:                 ->orderBy('km')
172:                 ->pluck('km')
173:                 ->map(fn ($v) => (int) $v)
174:                 ->unique()
175:                 ->values()
176:                 ->all();
177:         }
178: 
179:         foreach ($this->catalogCache[$brandKey] as $milestone) {
180:             if ($milestone >= $targetKm) {
181:                 return $milestone;
182:             }
183:         }
184: 
185:         return null;
186:     }
187: 
188:     private function classify(int $remainingKm): string
189:     {
190:         $critical = (int) config('oil.thresholds.critical_km', 1000);
191:         $dueSoon = (int) config('oil.thresholds.due_soon_km', 5000);
192: 
193:         return match (true) {
194:             $remainingKm < 0 => 'overdue',
195:             $remainingKm <= $critical => 'critical',
196:             $remainingKm <= $dueSoon => 'due-soon',
197:             default => 'ok',
198:         };
199:     }
200: }

 3: namespace App\Services\Onboarding;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Company;
 6: use App\Models\User;
 7: use App\Services\PivotAuditService;
 8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
10: use Illuminate\Support\Str;
11: 
12: /**
13:  * Handles atomic creation of a Company together with its first Director.
14:  */
15: class CompanyOnboardingService
16: {
17:     public function __construct(
18:         protected PivotAuditService $pivotAuditor
19:     ) {}
20: 
21:     public function createWithDirector(array $companyData, array $directorData): Company
22:     {
23:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($companyData, $directorData) {
24:             $company = Company::create([
25:                 'name' => $companyData['name'],
26:                 'slug' => $companyData['slug'],
27:                 'email' => $companyData['email'] ?? null,
28:                 'phone' => $companyData['phone'] ?? null,
29:                 'address' => $companyData['address'] ?? null,
30:                 'is_active' => $companyData['is_active'] ?? true,
31:             ]);
32: 
33:             $director = new User;
34:             $director->forceFill([
35:                 'name' => $directorData['name'],
36:                 'email' => $directorData['email'],
37:                 'password' => Hash::make($directorData['password']),
38:                 'employee_code' => $this->generateDirectorCode(),
39:                 'pin' => Hash::make($directorData['pin']),
40:                 'pin_is_default' => true,
41:                 'is_active' => true,
42:                 'email_verified_at' => now(), // ✅ Auto-verified: admin tərəfindən yaradılıb
43:             ])->save();
44: 
45:             $company->users()->attach($director->id, [
46:                 'role' => 'director',
47:                 'is_active' => true,
48:             ]);
49:             // The freshly-created director instance may be reused by
50:             // the caller in the same request (e.g. tests, seeders).
51:             // Clear any cached isDirector() result before returning.
52:             $director->forgetDirectorCache();
53: 
54:             // Audit: record the pivot attachment on the Company.
55:             $this->pivotAuditor->log(
56:                 subject: $company,
57:                 event: 'director_assigned',
58:                 oldValues: null,
59:                 newValues: ['director_id' => $director->id, 'director_name' => $director->name],
60:                 companyId: $company->id,
61:             );
62: 
63:             return $company->fresh(['directors']);
64:         });
65:     }
66: 
67:     private function generateDirectorCode(): string
68:     {
69:         do {
70:             $code = 'DIR-'.strtoupper(Str::random(6));
71:         } while (User::withTrashed()->where('employee_code', $code)->exists());
72: 
73:         return $code;
74:     }
75: }

 19:     /**
 20:      * Default complaint types created for every new garage.
 21:      *
 22:      * SuperAdmin can add or remove these through the UI later, but
 23:      * starting with a standard list means the "new complaint" form
 24:      * is usable the moment a garage is created.
 25:      */

 27:         'Engine noise',
 28:         'Tire puncture',
 29:         'Brake problem',
 30:         'Lighting failure',
 31:         'Transmission problem',
 32:         'Suspension problem',
 33:         'Electrical problem',
 34:         'Air conditioning failure',
 35:         'Oil leak',
 36:         'Other',
 37:     ];

 40:         protected PivotAuditService $pivotAuditor

 44:     {

 46:             $garage = Garage::create([
 47:                 'company_id' => $garageData['company_id'],
 48:                 'name' => $garageData['name'],
 49:                 'code' => $garageData['code'],
 50:                 'address' => $garageData['address'] ?? null,
 51:                 'phone' => $garageData['phone'] ?? null,
 52:                 'is_active' => $garageData['is_active'] ?? true,
 53:             ]);
 54: 
 55:             $admin = new User;
 56:             $admin->forceFill([
 57:                 'name' => $adminData['name'],
 58:                 'email' => $adminData['email'],
 59:                 'password' => Hash::make($adminData['password']),
 60:                 'employee_code' => $this->generateAdminCode(),
 61:                 'pin' => Hash::make($adminData['pin']),
 62:                 'pin_is_default' => true,
 63:                 'is_active' => true,
 64:                 'email_verified_at' => now(), // ✅ Auto-verified
 65:             ])->save();
 66:

 68:                 'role' => 'admin',
 69:                 'is_active' => true,
 70:             ]);
 71:

 73:             // Every garage starts with the standard catalog so the
 74:             // "new complaint" form works out of the box.

<file path="app/Services/PivotAuditService.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\AuditLog;
 6: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
 7: 
 8: /**
 9:  * Helper for logging audit entries on PIVOT table changes.
10:  *
11:  * Eloquent does not fire model events for pivot table operations
12:  * (`attach`, `detach`, `sync`, `updateExistingPivot`), so the Auditable
13:  * trait cannot see them. This service provides a single, consistent
14:  * entry point that all call sites use, so the audit shape stays uniform
15:  * and the logic is easy to find and review.
16:  *
17:  * Long-term alternative: custom events or a dedicated pivot model.
18:  * For now, explicit calls are simpler and more discoverable.
19:  */
20: class PivotAuditService
21: {
22:     /**
23:      * Record a pivot change in the audit log.
24:      *
25:      * @param  Model  $subject  The parent model the pivot belongs to
26:      *                          (Company for company_user, Garage for
27:      *                          garage_user, User for cross-references).
28:      * @param  string  $event  Semantic event name, e.g. 'director_assigned'.
29:      * @param  array|null  $oldValues  Previous state (null when newly attached).
30:      * @param  array|null  $newValues  New state (null when removed).
31:      * @param  int|null  $garageId  Garage context for the audit row.
32:      * @param  int|null  $companyId  Company context for the audit row.
33:      */
34:     public function log(
35:         Model $subject,
36:         string $event,
37:         ?array $oldValues = null,
38:         ?array $newValues = null,
39:         ?int $garageId = null,
40:         ?int $companyId = null,
41:     ): void {
42:         AuditLog::create([
43:             'user_id' => auth()->id(),
44:             'garage_id' => $garageId,
45:             'company_id' => $companyId,
46:             'auditable_type' => get_class($subject),
47:             'auditable_id' => $subject->getKey(),
48:             'event' => $event,
49:             'old_values' => $oldValues,
50:             'new_values' => $newValues,
51:         ]);
52:     }
53: }

<file path="app/Services/PostLoginRedirector.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\User;
 6: use Illuminate\Http\RedirectResponse;
 7: 
 8: /**
 9:  * Handles post-login navigation.
10:  *
11:  * Priority:
12:  *   1. Director (company-level)     → director.dashboard
13:  *   2. 0 active garages             → garage.selection (with error)
14:  *   3. 1 active garage              → auto-select + dashboard
15:  *   4. 2+ active garages            → garage.selection
16:  */
17: class PostLoginRedirector
18: {
19:     public static function redirect(User $user, string $routeName = 'dashboard'): RedirectResponse
20:     {
21:         // Directors operate at the company level and have their own dashboard.
22:         if ($user->isDirector()) {
23:             return redirect()->route('director.dashboard');
24:         }
25: 
26:         $activeGarages = $user->garages()
27:             ->wherePivot('is_active', true)
28:             ->with('company')
29:             ->get();
30: 
31:         if ($activeGarages->isEmpty()) {
32:             return redirect()->route('garage.selection')
33:                 ->with('error', __('messages.flash.no_garage_assigned'));
34:         }
35: 
36:         if ($activeGarages->count() === 1) {
37:             self::applyGarageContext($user, $activeGarages->first());
38: 
39:             return redirect()->intended(route($routeName, absolute: false));
40:         }
41: 
42:         return redirect()->route('garage.selection');
43:     }
44: 
45:     /**
46:      * Persist the given garage as the user's current garage.
47:      */
48:     public static function applyGarageContext(User $user, $garage): void
49:     {
50:         $user->update([
51:             'current_garage_id' => $garage->id,
52:             'current_company_id' => $garage->company_id,
53:             'last_selected_garage_at' => now(),
54:         ]);
55: 
56:         session([
57:             'current_garage_id' => $garage->id,
58:             'current_garage_name' => $garage->name,
59:             'current_company_id' => $garage->company_id,
60:             'current_company_name' => $garage->company?->name,
61:         ]);
62: 
63:         GarageContext::set($garage->id, $garage->company_id);
64:     }
65: }

<file path="app/Services/Reports/ComplaintReportService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\Reports;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\AuditLog;
  6: use App\Models\Complaint;
  7: use App\Models\User;
  8: use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
  9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 10: 
 11: class ComplaintReportService
 12: {
 13:     /**
 14:      * Summary of opened / closed cards within the period.
 15:      */
 16:     public function summary(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): array
 17:     {
 18:         $base = Complaint::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
 19:             ->whereIn('garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 20:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('created_by', $scope->userId))
 21:             ->when($scope->brandId, fn ($q) => $q->whereHas(
 22:                 'bus',
 23:                 fn ($bq) => $bq->where('brand_id', $scope->brandId)
 24:             ));
 25: 
 26:         $opened = (clone $base)
 27:             ->whereBetween('created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 28:             ->count();
 29: 
 30:         $closed = (clone $base)
 31:             ->whereNotNull('closed_at')
 32:             ->whereBetween('closed_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 33:             ->count();
 34: 
 35:         // ✅ FIX: Use the canonical open() scope so cancelled cards are
 36:         // excluded from the "open now" count.
 37:         //
 38:         // Previously this used `where('status', '!=', 'completed')`, which
 39:         // incorrectly counted CANCELLED complaints as open. That made the
 40:         // report disagree with the dashboard, which uses `Complaint::open()`
 41:         // (a scoped whereIn(['pending', 'in_progress'])).
 42:         $openNow = (clone $base)->open()->count();
 43: 
 44:         $byStatus = (clone $base)
 45:             ->whereBetween('created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 46:             ->select('status', DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total'))
 47:             ->groupBy('status')
 48:             ->pluck('total', 'status')
 49:             ->all();
 50: 
 51:         return [
 52:             'opened' => $opened,
 53:             'closed' => $closed,
 54:             'open_now' => $openNow,
 55:             'by_status' => $byStatus,
 56:         ];
 57:     }
 58: 
 59:     /**
 60:      * Top complaint types within the period.
 61:      */
 62:     public function topTypes(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
 63:     {
 64:         return Complaint::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
 65:             ->whereIn('garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 66:             ->whereBetween('created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 67:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('created_by', $scope->userId))
 68:             ->when($scope->brandId, fn ($q) => $q->whereHas(
 69:                 'bus',
 70:                 fn ($bq) => $bq->where('brand_id', $scope->brandId)
 71:             ))
 72:             ->select('complaint_type', DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total'))
 73:             ->whereNotNull('complaint_type')
 74:             ->groupBy('complaint_type')
 75:             ->orderByDesc('total')
 76:             ->get();
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     /**
 80:      * Per-user action counts based on the audit log.
 81:      *
 82:      * The brand filter is intentionally NOT applied here: worker
 83:      * activity counts how many actions each user performed, which is
 84:      * a user metric independent of which bus they touched.
 85:      */
 86:     public function workerActivity(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
 87:     {
 88:         $rows = AuditLog::query()
 89:             ->where('auditable_type', Complaint::class)
 90:             ->whereBetween('audit_logs.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 91:             ->whereIn('audit_logs.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 92:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('audit_logs.user_id', $scope->userId))
 93:             ->select(
 94:                 'user_id',
 95:                 DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total_actions'),
 96:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'created' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as created_count"),
 97:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'updated' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as updated_count"),
 98:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event IN ('deleted','force_deleted') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as deleted_count")
 99:             )
100:             ->groupBy('user_id')
101:             ->orderByDesc('total_actions')
102:             ->get();
103: 
104:         $users = User::whereIn('id', $rows->pluck('user_id')->filter()->all())
105:             ->get()
106:             ->keyBy('id');
107: 
108:         return $rows->map(fn ($row) => (object) [
109:             'user' => $users->get($row->user_id),
110:             'total_actions' => (int) $row->total_actions,
111:             'created_count' => (int) $row->created_count,
112:             'updated_count' => (int) $row->updated_count,
113:             'deleted_count' => (int) $row->deleted_count,
114:         ]);
115:     }
116: 
117:     /**
118:      * Complaint count per bus within the period.
119:      */
120:     public function byBus(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
121:     {
122:         return Complaint::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
123:             ->whereIn('complaints.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
124:             ->whereBetween('complaints.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
125:             ->whereNull('complaints.deleted_at')
126:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('complaints.created_by', $scope->userId))
127:             ->join('buses', 'buses.id', '=', 'complaints.bus_id')
128:             ->when($scope->brandId, fn ($q) => $q->where('buses.brand_id', $scope->brandId))
129:             ->select(
130:                 'buses.id as bus_id',
131:                 'buses.dqn',
132:                 'buses.route_number',
133:                 DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total'),
134:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN complaints.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as completed")
135:             )
136:             ->groupBy('buses.id', 'buses.dqn', 'buses.route_number')
137:             ->orderByDesc('total')
138:             ->limit(50)
139:             ->get();
140:     }
141: 
142:     /**
143:      * Average close time (in hours) for complaints closed in the period.
144:      */
145:     public function avgCloseTime(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): array
146:     {
147:         $rows = Complaint::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
148:             ->whereIn('garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
149:             ->whereNotNull('closed_at')
150:             ->whereBetween('closed_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
151:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('created_by', $scope->userId))
152:             ->when($scope->brandId, fn ($q) => $q->whereHas(
153:                 'bus',
154:                 fn ($bq) => $bq->where('brand_id', $scope->brandId)
155:             ))
156:             ->get(['created_at', 'closed_at', 'complaint_type']);
157: 
158:         if ($rows->isEmpty()) {
159:             return [
160:                 'overall_avg_hours' => null,
161:                 'sample_count' => 0,
162:                 'by_type' => collect(),
163:             ];
164:         }
165: 
166:         $durations = $rows->map(fn ($c) => $c->created_at->diffInHours($c->closed_at));
167: 
168:         $byType = $rows->groupBy('complaint_type')
169:             ->map(function ($group, $type) {
170:                 $hours = $group->map(fn ($c) => $c->created_at->diffInHours($c->closed_at));
171: 
172:                 return (object) [
173:                     'type' => $type,
174:                     'count' => $group->count(),
175:                     'avg_hours' => round($hours->avg(), 1),
176:                     'min_hours' => $hours->min(),
177:                     'max_hours' => $hours->max(),
178:                 ];
179:             })
180:             ->values();
181: 
182:         return [
183:             'overall_avg_hours' => round($durations->avg(), 1),
184:             'sample_count' => $rows->count(),
185:             'by_type' => $byType,
186:         ];
187:     }
188: }
