<file path="app/Services/Reports/WarehouseReportService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\Reports;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\AuditLog;
  6: use App\Models\ComplaintDetail;
  7: use App\Models\User;
  8: use App\Models\Warehouse;
  9: use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
 10: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 11: 
 12: class WarehouseReportService
 13: {
 14:     /**
 15:      * Items created within the period — a proxy for "receipts".
 16:      * (No dedicated stock movement table exists yet.)
 17:      */
 18:     public function receipt(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
 19:     {
 20:         return Warehouse::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
 21:             ->whereIn('garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 22:             ->whereBetween('created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 23:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('created_by', $scope->userId))
 24:             ->with('creator')
 25:             ->orderByDesc('created_at')
 26:             ->limit(500)
 27:             ->get();
 28:     }
 29: 
 30:     /**
 31:      * Top used parts across complaint details in the period.
 32:      * No user filter — this is a garage-wide usage report.
 33:      */
 34:     public function usage(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
 35:     {
 36:         return ComplaintDetail::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
 37:             ->whereIn('complaint_details.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 38:             ->whereNull('complaint_details.deleted_at')
 39:             ->whereHas('complaint', function ($q) use ($period) {
 40:                 $q->whereBetween('complaints.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 41:                     ->whereNull('complaints.deleted_at');
 42:             })
 43:             ->select(
 44:                 'code',
 45:                 DB::raw('MAX(name) as name'),
 46:                 DB::raw('SUM(used_quantity) as total_used'),
 47:                 DB::raw('COUNT(DISTINCT complaint_id) as times_used')
 48:             )
 49:             ->groupBy('code')
 50:             ->orderByDesc('total_used')
 51:             ->limit(50)
 52:             ->get();
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /**
 56:      * Per-user action counts based on the audit log.
 57:      */
 58:     public function workerActivity(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
 59:     {
 60:         $rows = AuditLog::query()
 61:             ->where('auditable_type', Warehouse::class)
 62:             ->whereBetween('audit_logs.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
 63:             ->whereIn('audit_logs.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 64:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('audit_logs.user_id', $scope->userId))
 65:             ->select(
 66:                 'user_id',
 67:                 DB::raw('COUNT(*) as total_actions'),
 68:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'created' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as created_count"),
 69:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event = 'updated' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as updated_count"),
 70:                 DB::raw("SUM(CASE WHEN event IN ('deleted','force_deleted') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as deleted_count")
 71:             )
 72:             ->groupBy('user_id')
 73:             ->orderByDesc('total_actions')
 74:             ->get();
 75: 
 76:         // Hydrate user objects in one query
 77:         $users = User::whereIn('id', $rows->pluck('user_id')->filter()->all())
 78:             ->get()
 79:             ->keyBy('id');
 80: 
 81:         return $rows->map(fn ($row) => (object) [
 82:             'user' => $users->get($row->user_id),
 83:             'total_actions' => (int) $row->total_actions,
 84:             'created_count' => (int) $row->created_count,
 85:             'updated_count' => (int) $row->updated_count,
 86:             'deleted_count' => (int) $row->deleted_count,
 87:         ]);
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     /**
 91:      * Current inventory below minimum threshold.
 92:      * No period filter — this is a current-state snapshot.
 93:      */
 94:     public function lowStock(ReportScope $scope): Collection
 95:     {
 96:         return Warehouse::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
 97:             ->whereIn('garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
 98:             ->whereColumn('quantity', '<=', 'minimum_quantity')
 99:             ->orderBy('quantity')
100:             ->orderBy('name')
101:             ->get();
102:     }
103: 
104:     /**
105:      * Raw audit log entries for Warehouse (per user, per period).
106:      */
107:     public function movement(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
108:     {
109:         return AuditLog::query()
110:             ->where('auditable_type', Warehouse::class)
111:             ->whereBetween('audit_logs.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
112:             ->whereIn('audit_logs.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
113:             ->when($scope->userId, fn ($q) => $q->where('audit_logs.user_id', $scope->userId))
114:             ->with('user')
115:             ->orderByDesc('audit_logs.id')
116:             ->limit(200)
117:             ->get();
118:     }
119: 
120:     /**
121:      * Per-vehicle part usage — "which service vehicle consumed how many
122:      * parts, and which parts specifically".
123:      *
124:      * Only counts complaint_details rows whose source_type is
125:      * 'service_vehicle' (i.e. parts that came off a service vehicle, not
126:      * off the warehouse). The complaint must have a linked vehicle;
127:      * legacy rows without one are ignored here.
128:      */
129:     public function serviceVehicleUsage(ReportPeriod $period, ReportScope $scope): Collection
130:     {
131:         return ComplaintDetail::withoutGlobalScope('garage')
132:             ->whereIn('complaint_details.garage_id', $scope->garageIds)
133:             ->whereNull('complaint_details.deleted_at')
134:             ->where('complaint_details.source_type', 'service_vehicle')
135:             ->whereHas('complaint', function ($q) use ($period) {
136:                 $q->whereBetween('complaints.created_at', [$period->from, $period->to])
137:                     ->whereNull('complaints.deleted_at')
138:                     ->whereNotNull('complaints.service_vehicle_id');
139:             })
140:             ->join('complaints', 'complaints.id', '=', 'complaint_details.complaint_id')
141:             ->join('service_vehicles', 'service_vehicles.id', '=', 'complaints.service_vehicle_id')
142:             ->select(
143:                 'service_vehicles.id as service_vehicle_id',
144:                 'service_vehicles.name as service_vehicle_name',
145:                 'service_vehicles.plate_number as service_vehicle_plate',
146:                 'complaint_details.code',
147:                 DB::raw('MAX(complaint_details.name) as part_name'),
148:                 DB::raw('SUM(complaint_details.used_quantity) as total_used'),
149:                 DB::raw('COUNT(DISTINCT complaint_details.complaint_id) as times_used')
150:             )
151:             ->groupBy(
152:                 'service_vehicles.id',
153:                 'service_vehicles.name',
154:                 'service_vehicles.plate_number',
155:                 'complaint_details.code'
156:             )
157:             ->orderBy('service_vehicles.name')
158:             ->orderByDesc('total_used')
159:             ->get();
160:     }
161: }
</file>

<file path="app/Services/UserService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\User;
  6: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
  7: 
  8: class UserService
  9: {
 10:     public function __construct(
 11:         protected PivotAuditService $pivotAuditor
 12:     ) {}
 13: 
 14:     /**
 15:      * Create a new user and attach them to the given garage.
 16:      *
 17:      * Every step runs inside a single transaction — all or nothing,
 18:      * so a half-created user can never end up in the database.
 19:      */
 20:     public function createUserWithGarageRole(
 21:         array $data,
 22:         int $garageId,
 23:         bool $isActive = true
 24:     ): User {
 25:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($data, $garageId, $isActive) {
 26:             $user = new User;
 27:             $user->forceFill([
 28:                 'name' => $data['name'],
 29:                 'email' => $data['email'],
 30:                 'password' => $data['password'],
 31:                 'email_verified_at' => now(), // ✅ Auto-verified: qaraj admini yaradıb
 32:             ])->save();
 33: 
 34:             $user->garages()->attach($garageId, [
 35:                 'role' => $data['role'],
 36:                 'is_active' => $isActive,
 37:             ]);
 38: 
 39:             // Audit: record the garage pivot assignment.
 40:             $this->pivotAuditor->log(
 41:                 subject: $user,
 42:                 event: 'garage_role_assigned',
 43:                 oldValues: null,
 44:                 newValues: ['garage_id' => $garageId, 'role' => $data['role'], 'is_active' => $isActive],
 45:                 garageId: $garageId,
 46:             );
 47: 
 48:             $user->forgetRoleCache();
 49: 
 50:             return $user;
 51:         });
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     /**
 55:      * Update the user's profile and their garage role.
 56:      */
 57:     public function updateUserWithGarageRole(
 58:         User $user,
 59:         array $data,
 60:         int $garageId
 61:     ): User {
 62:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($user, $data, $garageId) {
 63:             $userUpdate = [
 64:                 'name' => $data['name'],
 65:                 'email' => $data['email'],
 66:             ];
 67: 
 68:             if (! empty($data['password'])) {
 69:                 $userUpdate['password'] = $data['password'];
 70:             }
 71: 
 72:             // Capture the previous pivot state for audit purposes.
 73:             $previousPivot = $user->garages()
 74:                 ->whereKey($garageId)
 75:                 ->first()?->pivot;
 76: 
 77:             $oldPivotValues = $previousPivot ? [
 78:                 'role' => $previousPivot->role,
 79:                 'is_active' => (bool) $previousPivot->is_active,
 80:             ] : null;
 81: 
 82:             $user->update($userUpdate);
 83: 
 84:             $user->garages()->updateExistingPivot($garageId, [
 85:                 'role' => $data['role'],
 86:                 'is_active' => $data['is_active'],
 87:             ]);
 88: 
 89:             // Audit: record the pivot update only when something changed.
 90:             $newPivotValues = [
 91:                 'role' => $data['role'],
 92:                 'is_active' => (bool) $data['is_active'],
 93:             ];
 94: 
 95:             $pivotChanged = $oldPivotValues === null
 96:                 || $oldPivotValues['role'] !== $newPivotValues['role']
 97:                 || $oldPivotValues['is_active'] !== $newPivotValues['is_active'];
 98: 
 99:             if ($pivotChanged) {
100:                 $this->pivotAuditor->log(
101:                     subject: $user,
102:                     event: 'garage_role_updated',
103:                     oldValues: $oldPivotValues,
104:                     newValues: $newPivotValues,
105:                     garageId: $garageId,
106:                 );
107:             }
108: 
109:             $user->forgetRoleCache();
110: 
111:             return $user->fresh(['garages']);
112:         });
113:     }
114: }

<file path="app/Services/Warehouse/WarehouseTransferService.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Services\Warehouse;
  4: 
  5: use App\Enums\TransferStatus;
  6: use App\Enums\TransferType;
  7: use App\Models\Garage;
  8: use App\Models\ServiceVehicleStock;
  9: use App\Models\Warehouse;
 10: use App\Models\WarehouseTransfer;
 11: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 12: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
 13: use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
 14: 
 15: /**
 16:  * Business logic for warehouse transfers.
 17:  *
 18:  * All stock mutations happen inside a DB transaction with row-level
 19:  * locking (lockForUpdate) so two concurrent transfers can never
 20:  * oversell the same stock.
 21:  *
 22:  * The service is deliberately unaware of HTTP concerns — no
 23:  * redirects, no session, no request. Controllers handle those.
 24:  */
 25: class WarehouseTransferService
 26: {
 27:     /**
 28:      * Create a new transfer in draft state.
 29:      *
 30:      * @param  array{
 31:      *     from_garage_id: int,
 32:      *     to_garage_id?: int|null,
 33:      *     to_service_vehicle_id?: int|null,
 34:      *     type: string,
 35:      *     notes?: string|null,
 36:      *     items: array<int, array{warehouse_id: int, declared_quantity: int, notes?: string|null}>,
 37:      * }  $data
 38:      */
 39:     public function create(array $data, int $companyId): WarehouseTransfer
 40:     {
 41:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($data, $companyId) {
 42:             $type = TransferType::from($data['type']);
 43: 
 44:             // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 45:             // SECURITY GUARD: cross-company / cross-garage destination
 46:             //
 47:             // The FormRequest already validates this, but we re-check
 48:             // here as defense-in-depth. If a future controller, job,
 49:             // or console command calls this service directly, it must
 50:             // not be possible to inject stock into a foreign tenant.
 51:             // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 52:             if ($type->isGarageToGarage() && ! empty($data['to_garage_id'])) {
 53:                 $destinationGarage = Garage::withoutGlobalScopes()
 54:                     ->whereKey($data['to_garage_id'])
 55:                     ->where('company_id', $companyId)
 56:                     ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 57:                     ->first();
 58: 
 59:                 if (! $destinationGarage) {
 60:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
 61:                         'to_garage_id' => __('validation.exists', [
 62:                             'attribute' => __('messages.transfers.to_garage'),
 63:                         ]),
 64:                     ]);
 65:                 }
 66:             }
 67: 
 68:             if ($type->isToServiceVehicle() && ! empty($data['to_service_vehicle_id'])) {
 69:                 $vehicleExists = \App\Models\ServiceVehicle::withoutGlobalScopes()
 70:                     ->whereKey($data['to_service_vehicle_id'])
 71:                     ->where('garage_id', $data['from_garage_id'])
 72:                     ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 73:                     ->exists();
 74: 
 75:                 if (! $vehicleExists) {
 76:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
 77:                         'to_service_vehicle_id' => __('validation.exists', [
 78:                             'attribute' => __('messages.transfers.to_service_vehicle'),
 79:                         ]),
 80:                     ]);
 81:                 }
 82:             }
 83: 
 84:             // Item rows must exist and belong to the source garage.
 85:             // We lock them now so nobody can delete them mid-create.
 86:             //
 87:             // Quarantine rows are explicitly excluded: defective parts
 88:             // must never enter the normal transfer workflow — they are
 89:             // reserved for inspection, disposal, or the dedicated
 90:             // return-to-quarantine transfer type.
 91:             $warehouseIds = array_column($data['items'], 'warehouse_id');
 92: 
 93:             $warehouses = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
 94:                 ->whereIn('id', $warehouseIds)
 95:                 ->where('garage_id', $data['from_garage_id'])
 96:                 ->where('is_quarantine', false)
 97:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
 98:                 ->lockForUpdate()
 99:                 ->get()
100:                 ->keyBy('id');
101: 
102:             if ($warehouses->count() !== count(array_unique($warehouseIds))) {
103:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
104:                     'items' => __('messages.transfers.invalid_warehouse_items'),
105:                 ]);
106:             }
107: 
108:             $total = 0;
109:             foreach ($data['items'] as $item) {
110:                 $total += (int) $item['declared_quantity'];
111:             }
112: 
113:             $transfer = WarehouseTransfer::create([
114:                 'company_id' => $companyId,
115:                 'from_garage_id' => $data['from_garage_id'],
116:                 'to_garage_id' => $type->isGarageToGarage() ? $data['to_garage_id'] : null,
117:                 'to_service_vehicle_id' => $type->isToServiceVehicle() ? $data['to_service_vehicle_id'] : null,
118:                 'type' => $type->value,
119:                 'status' => TransferStatus::Draft->value,
120:                 'declared_total' => $total,
121:                 'notes' => $data['notes'] ?? null,
122:                 'created_by' => auth()->id(),
123:             ]);
124: 
125:             foreach ($data['items'] as $item) {
126:                 $transfer->items()->create([
127:                     'warehouse_id' => $item['warehouse_id'],
128:                     'declared_quantity' => (int) $item['declared_quantity'],
129:                     'notes' => $item['notes'] ?? null,
130:                 ]);
131:             }
132: 
133:             return $transfer->fresh(['items']);
134:         });
135:     }
136: 
137:     /**
138:      * Dispatch a draft transfer: decrement stock on the source garage
139:      * and move the transfer to "dispatched".
140:      *
141:      * ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
142:      * The transfer row is locked FIRST inside the transaction, and the
143:      * status check runs AFTER the lock is held. Two concurrent dispatch
144:      * requests for the same transfer are therefore serialized: the
145:      * second request sees the updated status (dispatched) and is
146:      * rejected before touching stock.
147:      *
148:      * Without this lock, both requests would pass the initial status
149:      * check, then both would decrement the source stock — a double-
150:      * deduction that corrupts inventory.
151:      *
152:      * Items are sorted by warehouse_id before any warehouse lock is
153:      * acquired to eliminate deadlocks between concurrent transfers
154:      * that reference the same warehouses in different orders.
155:      */
156:     public function dispatch(WarehouseTransfer $transfer): void
157:     {
158:         DB::transaction(function () use ($transfer) {
159:             // ── Lock the transfer row FIRST ──
160:             $locked = WarehouseTransfer::withoutGlobalScopes()
161:                 ->whereKey($transfer->getKey())
162:                 ->lockForUpdate()
163:                 ->firstOrFail();
164: 
165:             if (! $locked->status->isDraft()) {
166:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
167:                     'status' => __('messages.transfers.cannot_dispatch'),
168:                 ]);
169:             }
170: 
171:             $locked->load('items.warehouse');
172: 
173:             // ── Deterministic lock order for warehouses ──
174:             $sortedItems = $locked->items
175:                 ->sortBy('warehouse_id')
176:                 ->values();
177: 
178:             foreach ($sortedItems as $item) {
179:                 $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
180:                     ->where('id', $item->warehouse_id)
181:                     ->where('is_quarantine', false)
182:                     ->whereNull('deleted_at')
183:                     ->lockForUpdate()
184:                     ->first();
185: 
186:                 if (! $warehouse) {
187:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
188:                         'items' => __('messages.flash.stock_item_not_found', [
189:                             'code' => $item->warehouse?->code ?? '—',
190:                         ]),
191:                     ]);
192:                 }
193: 
194:                 if ($warehouse->quantity < $item->declared_quantity) {
195:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
196:                         'items' => __('messages.flash.stock_insufficient', [
197:                             'name' => $warehouse->name,
198:                             'requested' => $item->declared_quantity,
199:                             'available' => $warehouse->quantity,
200:                         ]),
201:                     ]);
202:                 }
203: 
204:                 $warehouse->decrement('quantity', $item->declared_quantity);
205:             }
206: 
207:             $locked->update([
208:                 'status' => TransferStatus::Dispatched->value,
209:                 'dispatched_by' => auth()->id(),
210:                 'dispatched_at' => now(),
211:             ]);
212:         });
213:     }
214: 
215:     /**
216:      * Receive a dispatched transfer.
217:      *
218:      * ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
219:      * Same pattern as dispatch(): the transfer row is locked first,
220:      * the status is re-checked under the lock. Two concurrent receive
221:      * requests would otherwise both pass the "isDispatched" check and
222:      * both increment destination stock — a double-credit.
223:      *
224:      * Destination warehouse rows are locked in `warehouse_id` order
225:      * to eliminate deadlocks between concurrent transfers.
226:      *
227:      * ── SURPLUS GUARD ──
228:      * The source garage only ever dispatched `declared` units, and
229:      * dispatch() already deducted exactly that many from the source
230:      * stock. Crediting MORE than `declared` to the destination would
231:      * create stock out of thin air — the exact same physical unit
232:      * would be counted in two places at once.
233:      *
234:      * @param  array<int, int>  $receivedQuantities  [transfer_item_id => received_qty]
235:      */
236:     public function receive(WarehouseTransfer $transfer, array $receivedQuantities): void
237:     {
238:         DB::transaction(function () use ($transfer, $receivedQuantities) {
239:             // ── Lock the transfer row FIRST ──
240:             $locked = WarehouseTransfer::withoutGlobalScopes()
241:                 ->whereKey($transfer->getKey())
242:                 ->lockForUpdate()
243:                 ->firstOrFail();
244: 
245:             if (! $locked->status->isDispatched()) {
246:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
247:                     'status' => __('messages.transfers.cannot_receive'),
248:                 ]);
249:             }
250: 
251:             $locked->load('items');
252: 
253:             $receivedTotal = 0;
254:             $hasDiscrepancy = false;
255:             $discrepancies = [];
256: 
257:             // ── Deterministic lock order for destination warehouses ──
258:             $sortedItems = $locked->items
259:                 ->sortBy('warehouse_id')
260:                 ->values();
261: 
262:             foreach ($sortedItems as $item) {
263:                 $received = $receivedQuantities[$item->id] ?? null;
264: 
265:                 if ($received === null) {
266:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
267:                         'received' => __('messages.transfers.missing_received_quantity'),
268:                     ]);
269:                 }
270: 
271:                 $received = (int) $received;
272: 
273:                 if ($received < 0) {
274:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
275:                         'received' => __('messages.transfers.negative_quantity'),
276:                     ]);
277:                 }
278: 
279:                 // ── SURPLUS GUARD ──
280:                 // The source garage only ever dispatched `declared`
281:                 // units and the dispatch step already deducted exactly
282:                 // that many from the source stock. Crediting MORE than
283:                 // `declared` to the destination would create stock out
284:                 // of thin air — the exact same physical unit would be
285:                 // counted in two places at once.
286:                 if ($received > $item->declared_quantity) {
287:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
288:                         'received' => __('messages.transfers.received_exceeds_declared', [
289:                             'declared' => $item->declared_quantity,
290:                             'received' => $received,
291:                         ]),
292:                     ]);
293:                 }
294: 
295:                 $item->update(['received_quantity' => $received]);
296:                 $receivedTotal += $received;
297: 
298:                 $diff = $received - $item->declared_quantity;
299: 
300:                 if ($diff !== 0) {
301:                     $hasDiscrepancy = true;
302: 
303:                     $itemLabel = $item->warehouse?->code
304:                         ? $item->warehouse->code.' — '.($item->warehouse->name ?? '')
305:                         : "Item #{$item->id}";
306: 
307:                     $discrepancies[] = sprintf(
308:                         '%s: declared %d, received %d (%+d)',
309:                         $itemLabel,
310:                         $item->declared_quantity,
311:                         $received,
312:                         $diff
313:                     );
314:                 }
315: 
316:                 if ($received > 0) {
317:                     $this->incrementDestinationStock($locked, $item->warehouse_id, $received);
318:                 }
319:             }
320: 
321:             $newStatus = $hasDiscrepancy
322:                 ? TransferStatus::Disputed->value
323:                 : TransferStatus::Received->value;
324: 
325:             $locked->update([
326:                 'status' => $newStatus,
327:                 'received_total' => $receivedTotal,
328:                 'discrepancy_notes' => $hasDiscrepancy
329:                     ? implode("\n", $discrepancies)
330:                     : null,
331:                 'received_by' => auth()->id(),
332:                 'received_at' => now(),
333:             ]);
334:         });
335:     }
336: 
337:     /**
338:      * Reject a dispatched transfer entirely.
339:      * All quantities are returned to the source garage.
340:      *
341:      * ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
342:      * The transfer row is locked first, the status is re-checked under
343:      * the lock. Two concurrent rejects would otherwise both restore the
344:      * source stock — a double-credit.
345:      *
346:      * Source warehouse rows are locked in `warehouse_id` order to
347:      * eliminate deadlocks.
348:      */
349:     public function reject(WarehouseTransfer $transfer, ?string $reason = null): void
350:     {
351:         DB::transaction(function () use ($transfer, $reason) {
352:             // ── Lock the transfer row FIRST ──
353:             $locked = WarehouseTransfer::withoutGlobalScopes()
354:                 ->whereKey($transfer->getKey())
355:                 ->lockForUpdate()
356:                 ->firstOrFail();
357: 
358:             if (! $locked->status->isDispatched()) {
359:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
360:                     'status' => __('messages.transfers.cannot_reject'),
361:                 ]);
362:             }
363: 
364:             $locked->load('items');
365: 
366:             // ── Deterministic lock order for source warehouses ──
367:             $sortedItems = $locked->items
368:                 ->sortBy('warehouse_id')
369:                 ->values();
370: 
371:             foreach ($sortedItems as $item) {
372:                 $warehouse = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
373:                     ->where('id', $item->warehouse_id)
374:                     ->lockForUpdate()
375:                     ->first();
376: 
377:                 if ($warehouse) {
378:                     $warehouse->increment('quantity', $item->declared_quantity);
379:                 }
380:             }
381: 
382:             $locked->update([
383:                 'status' => TransferStatus::Rejected->value,
384:                 'received_total' => 0,
385:                 'discrepancy_notes' => $reason,
386:                 'received_by' => auth()->id(),
387:                 'received_at' => now(),
388:             ]);
389:         });
390:     }
391: 
392:     /**
393:      * Resolve a disputed transfer.
394:      *
395:      * ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
396:      * The transfer row is locked first, the status is re-checked under
397:      * the lock. Two concurrent resolves (one choosing `retransfer`, the
398:      * other `loss_accepted`) would otherwise both succeed and corrupt
399:      * the state — e.g. create TWO follow-up drafts.
400:      *
401:      * @param  string  $resolution  'retransfer' or 'loss_accepted'
402:      */
403:     public function resolveDisputed(WarehouseTransfer $transfer, string $resolution): void
404:     {
405:         DB::transaction(function () use ($transfer, $resolution) {
406:             // ── Lock the transfer row FIRST ──
407:             $locked = WarehouseTransfer::withoutGlobalScopes()
408:                 ->whereKey($transfer->getKey())
409:                 ->lockForUpdate()
410:                 ->firstOrFail();
411: 
412:             if (! $locked->status->isDisputed()) {
413:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
414:                     'status' => __('messages.transfers.cannot_resolve'),
415:                 ]);
416:             }
417: 
418:             if (! in_array($resolution, ['retransfer', 'loss_accepted'], true)) {
419:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
420:                     'resolution' => __('messages.transfers.invalid_resolution'),
421:                 ]);
422:             }
423: 
424:             $locked->load('items');
425: 
426:             if ($resolution === 'retransfer') {
427:                 $missingItems = [];
428:                 $nullReceived = [];
429: 
430:                 foreach ($locked->items as $item) {
431:                     if ($item->received_quantity === null) {
432:                         $nullReceived[] = $item->id;
433:                     }
434: 
435:                     $missing = $item->declared_quantity - ($item->received_quantity ?? 0);
436: 
437:                     if ($missing > 0) {
438:                         $missingItems[] = [
439:                             'warehouse_id' => $item->warehouse_id,
440:                             'declared_quantity' => $missing,
441:                             'notes' => __('messages.transfers.retransfer_note', [
442:                                 'original' => $locked->id,
443:                             ]),
444:                         ];
445:                     }
446:                 }
447: 
448:                 if (! empty($nullReceived)) {
449:                     Log::warning('Disputed transfer has items with null received_quantity', [
450:                         'transfer_id' => $locked->id,
451:                         'item_ids' => $nullReceived,
452:                     ]);
453:                 }
454: 
455:                 if (empty($missingItems)) {
456:                     Log::info('Retransfer requested but no missing items found', [
457:                         'transfer_id' => $locked->id,
458:                     ]);
459:                 } else {
460:                     // Nested create() acquires its own locks on source
461:                     // warehouses. Sorting is inherited from dispatch()'s
462:                     // deterministic lock order pattern.
463:                     $this->create([
464:                         'from_garage_id' => $locked->from_garage_id,
465:                         'to_garage_id' => $locked->to_garage_id,
466:                         'to_service_vehicle_id' => $locked->to_service_vehicle_id,
467:                         'type' => $locked->type->value,
468:                         'notes' => __('messages.transfers.retransfer_note', ['original' => $locked->id]),
469:                         'items' => $missingItems,
470:                     ], $locked->company_id);
471:                 }
472:             }
473: 
474:             $locked->update([
475:                 'status' => TransferStatus::Resolved->value,
476:                 'resolution' => $resolution,
477:                 'resolved_by' => auth()->id(),
478:                 'resolved_at' => now(),
479:             ]);
480:         });
481:     }
482: 
483:     /**
484:      * Cancel a draft transfer. No stock has been touched at this point,
485:      * so nothing to restore.
486:      *
487:      * ── CONCURRENCY GUARD ──
488:      * Even though no stock is mutated, the status check must be
489:      * serialized: without the row lock, a concurrent dispatch could
490:      * transition the transfer to "dispatched" while this cancel() is
491:      * still deciding — and cancel() would then mark a dispatched
492:      * transfer as cancelled, orphaning the stock that was already
493:      * deducted by the other request.
494:      */
495:     public function cancel(WarehouseTransfer $transfer): void
496:     {
497:         DB::transaction(function () use ($transfer) {
498:             // ── Lock the transfer row FIRST ──
499:             $locked = WarehouseTransfer::withoutGlobalScopes()
500:                 ->whereKey($transfer->getKey())
501:                 ->lockForUpdate()
502:                 ->firstOrFail();
503: 
504:             if (! $locked->status->isDraft()) {
505:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
506:                     'status' => __('messages.transfers.cannot_cancel'),
507:                 ]);
508:             }
509: 
510:             $locked->update(['status' => TransferStatus::Cancelled->value]);
511:         });
512:     }
513: 
514:     // ==================== PRIVATE ====================
515: 
516:     /**
517:      * Increment the destination's stock for the given item.
518:      *
519:      * For garage-to-garage transfers, the destination warehouse row
520:      * is the SAME code within the destination garage — we look it up
521:      * or create it on the fly.
522:      */
523:     private function incrementDestinationStock(WarehouseTransfer $transfer, int $sourceWarehouseId, int $quantity): void
524:     {
525:         if (! $transfer->to_garage_id) {
526:             return; // Service-vehicle / quarantine: handled elsewhere.
527:         }
528: 
529:         $source = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
530:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
531:             ->find($sourceWarehouseId);
532: 
533:         if (! $source) {
534:             return;
535:         }
536: 
537:         $destination = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
538:             ->where('garage_id', $transfer->to_garage_id)
539:             ->where('code', $source->code)
540:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
541:             ->lockForUpdate()
542:             ->first();
543: 
544:         if ($destination) {
545:             $destination->increment('quantity', $quantity);
546: 
547:             return;
548:         }
549: 
550:         // The destination garage does not yet have this item.
551:         // Create it from the source row, preserving code/name/unit/
552:         // price/minimum_quantity so the two rows stay aligned.
553:         //
554:         // ✅ SECURITY: We set company_id from the DESTINATION garage,
555:         // not from the transfer's company_id. This keeps the warehouse
556:         // row internally consistent even if the transfer data were
557:         // somehow corrupted upstream.
558:         $destinationGarage = Garage::withoutGlobalScopes()
559:             ->whereKey($transfer->to_garage_id)
560:             ->first();
561: 
562:         Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()->create([
563:             'garage_id' => $transfer->to_garage_id,
564:             'company_id' => $destinationGarage?->company_id ?? $transfer->company_id,
565:             'code' => $source->code,
566:             'name' => $source->name,
567:             'category' => $source->category,
568:             'unit' => $source->unit,
569:             'quantity' => $quantity,
570:             'minimum_quantity' => $source->minimum_quantity,
571:             'price' => $source->price,
572:             'supplier' => $source->supplier,
573:         ]);
574:     }
575: 
576:     /**
577:      * Create AND immediately complete a transfer that does not
578:      * require the dispatch → receive workflow.
579:      *
580:      * Currently used for:
581:      *   - return_to_quarantine (within the same garage)
582:      *   - to_service_vehicle
583:      */
584:     public function createAndComplete(array $data, int $companyId): WarehouseTransfer
585:     {
586:         $type = TransferType::from($data['type']);
587: 
588:         if ($type->requiresWorkflow()) {
589:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
590:                 'type' => __('messages.transfers.type_requires_workflow'),
591:             ]);
592:         }
593: 
594:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($data, $companyId, $type) {
595:             // SECURITY: same-vehicle guard as in create().
596:             if ($type->isToServiceVehicle() && ! empty($data['to_service_vehicle_id'])) {
597:                 $vehicleExists = \App\Models\ServiceVehicle::withoutGlobalScopes()
598:                     ->whereKey($data['to_service_vehicle_id'])
599:                     ->where('garage_id', $data['from_garage_id'])
600:                     ->whereNull('deleted_at')
601:                     ->exists();
602: 
603:                 if (! $vehicleExists) {
604:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
605:                         'to_service_vehicle_id' => __('validation.exists', [
606:                             'attribute' => __('messages.transfers.to_service_vehicle'),
607:                         ]),
608:                     ]);
609:                 }
610:             }
611: 
612:             $warehouseIds = array_column($data['items'], 'warehouse_id');
613: 
614:             $warehouses = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
615:                 ->whereIn('id', $warehouseIds)
616:                 ->where('garage_id', $data['from_garage_id'])
617:                 ->where('is_quarantine', false)
618:                 ->whereNull('deleted_at')
619:                 ->lockForUpdate()
620:                 ->get()
621:                 ->keyBy('id');
622: 
623:             if ($warehouses->count() !== count(array_unique($warehouseIds))) {
624:                 throw ValidationException::withMessages([
625:                     'items' => __('messages.transfers.invalid_warehouse_items'),
626:                 ]);
627:             }
628: 
629:             $total = 0;
630:             foreach ($data['items'] as $item) {
631:                 $total += (int) $item['declared_quantity'];
632:             }
633: 
634:             $transfer = WarehouseTransfer::create([
635:                 'company_id' => $companyId,
636:                 'from_garage_id' => $data['from_garage_id'],
637:                 'to_garage_id' => null,
638:                 'to_service_vehicle_id' => $type->isToServiceVehicle() ? ($data['to_service_vehicle_id'] ?? null) : null,
639:                 'type' => $type->value,
640:                 'status' => TransferStatus::Received->value,
641:                 'declared_total' => $total,
642:                 'received_total' => $total,
643:                 'notes' => $data['notes'] ?? null,
644:                 'created_by' => auth()->id(),
645:                 'dispatched_by' => auth()->id(),
646:                 'dispatched_at' => now(),
647:                 'received_by' => auth()->id(),
648:                 'received_at' => now(),
649:             ]);
650: 
651:             foreach ($data['items'] as $item) {
652:                 $source = $warehouses->get($item['warehouse_id']);
653: 
654:                 if ($source->quantity < $item['declared_quantity']) {
655:                     throw ValidationException::withMessages([
656:                         'items' => __('messages.flash.stock_insufficient', [
657:                             'name' => $source->name,
658:                             'requested' => $item['declared_quantity'],
659:                             'available' => $source->quantity,
660:                         ]),
661:                     ]);
662:                 }
663: 
664:                 $transfer->items()->create([
665:                     'warehouse_id' => $source->id,
666:                     'declared_quantity' => $item['declared_quantity'],
667:                     'received_quantity' => $item['declared_quantity'],
668:                     'notes' => $item['notes'] ?? null,
669:                 ]);
670: 
671:                 $source->decrement('quantity', $item['declared_quantity']);
672: 
673:                 if ($type->isReturnToQuarantine()) {
674:                     $this->moveToQuarantine($source, $item['declared_quantity']);
675:                 } elseif ($type->isToServiceVehicle()) {
676:                     $this->moveToServiceVehicle(
677:                         $transfer->to_service_vehicle_id,
678:                         $source,
679:                         $item['declared_quantity']
680:                     );
681:                 }
682:             }
683: 
684:             return $transfer->fresh(['items']);
685:         });
686:     }
687: 
688:     /**
689:      * Move `quantity` units of the given source warehouse item to its
690:      * matching quarantine row in the SAME garage.
691:      */
692:     private function moveToQuarantine(Warehouse $source, int $quantity): void
693:     {
694:         $quarantineCode = 'Q-'.$source->code;
695: 
696:         $quarantine = Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()
697:             ->where('garage_id', $source->garage_id)
698:             ->where('code', $quarantineCode)
699:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
700:             ->lockForUpdate()
701:             ->first();
702: 
703:         if ($quarantine) {
704:             $quarantine->increment('quantity', $quantity);
705: 
706:             return;
707:         }
708: 
709:         Warehouse::withoutGlobalScopes()->create([
710:             'garage_id' => $source->garage_id,
711:             'company_id' => $source->company_id,
712:             'code' => $quarantineCode,
713:             'name' => $source->name,
714:             'category' => $source->category,
715:             'unit' => $source->unit,
716:             'is_quarantine' => true,
717:             'quantity' => $quantity,
718:             'minimum_quantity' => 0,
719:             'price' => $source->price,
720:             'supplier' => $source->supplier,
721:         ]);
722:     }
723: 
724:     /**
725:      * Move `quantity` units of the given source warehouse item to
726:      * the stock of the target service vehicle.
727:      */
728:     private function moveToServiceVehicle(int $serviceVehicleId, Warehouse $source, int $quantity): void
729:     {
730:         $stock = ServiceVehicleStock::withoutGlobalScopes()
731:             ->where('service_vehicle_id', $serviceVehicleId)
732:             ->where('code', $source->code)
733:             ->lockForUpdate()
734:             ->first();
735: 
736:         if ($stock) {
737:             $stock->increment('quantity', $quantity);
738: 
739:             return;
740:         }
741: 
742:         ServiceVehicleStock::withoutGlobalScopes()->create([
743:             'service_vehicle_id' => $serviceVehicleId,
744:             'garage_id' => $source->garage_id,
745:             'company_id' => $source->company_id,
746:             'code' => $source->code,
747:             'name' => $source->name,
748:             'category' => $source->category,
749:             'unit' => $source->unit,
750:             'quantity' => $quantity,
751:         ]);
752:     }
753: }

<file path="app/Support/Auth/TimingAttackDefense.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Support\Auth;
 4: 
 5: /**
 6:  * Timing-attack defense helpers for authentication.
 7:  *
 8:  * WHEN A LOGIN TARGETS A NONEXISTENT CREDENTIAL
 9:  * ---------------------------------------------
10:  * A naive login controller returns immediately when the email or
11:  * employee code does not exist:
12:  *
13:  *     $user = User::where('email', $email)->first();
14:  *     if (! $user) {
15:  *         return back()->withErrors(['email' => 'Invalid credentials']);
16:  *     }
17:  *
18:  * That branch returns in microseconds — no bcrypt check, no DB
19:  * round-trip beyond the initial SELECT. A successful "user exists"
20:  * branch, by contrast, runs a bcrypt comparison that takes tens of
21:  * milliseconds. The difference is measurable over the network, and
22:  * an attacker can enumerate valid emails by timing the response:
23:  *
24:  *     for each candidate email:
25:  *         t0 = now()
26:  *         POST /login  {email, password: "anything"}
27:  *         t1 = now()
28:  *         if (t1 - t0) > 50ms: email exists
29:  *
30:  * HOW THIS HELPER DEFEATS THAT
31:  * ----------------------------
32:  * We always run a bcrypt comparison, even when the user is missing,
33:  * by falling back to this constant hash. The comparison always fails
34:  * (the dummy hash is not the hash of any user's password), but the
35:  * timing profile of the two branches becomes indistinguishable.
36:  *
37:  * THE VALUE BELOW
38:  * ---------------
39:  * It is the bcrypt hash of the literal string "password" — the same
40:  * value Laravel's UserFactory generates by default. It contains no
41:  * real secret and is safe to commit to source control.
42:  */
43: final class TimingAttackDefense
44: {
45:     /**
46:      * A valid bcrypt hash used as a comparison target when the
47:      * submitted credential does not match any user.
48:      *
49:      * NEVER replace this with a hash of a real password. Its only
50:      * purpose is to burn CPU cycles in a way that is timing-identical
51:      * to a genuine "wrong password" check.
52:      */
53:     public const DUMMY_HASH = '$2y$10$92IXUNpkjO0rOQ5byMi.Ye4oKoEa3Ro9llC/.og/at2.uheWG/igi';
54: }
</file>

<file path="app/Support/Excel/SafeCell.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Support\Excel;
 4: 
 5: /**
 6:  * Sanitizes user-controlled strings before writing them into an
 7:  * Excel/CSV cell.
 8:  *
 9:  * Excel treats values starting with =, +, -, @, tab, or CR as
10:  * formulas. When a user exports a driver named "=HYPERLINK(...)"
11:  * and someone opens the file, the formula executes.
12:  *
13:  * This helper prefixes any suspicious value with a single quote,
14:  * which Excel interprets as "treat the rest as literal text".
15:  */
16: final class SafeCell
17: {
18:     private const DANGEROUS_PREFIXES = ['=', '+', '-', '@', "\t", "\r"];
19: 
20:     public static function sanitize(mixed $value): mixed
21:     {
22:         if (! is_string($value)) {
23:             return $value;
24:         }
25: 
26:         if ($value === '') {
27:             return $value;
28:         }
29: 
30:         // Strip control characters that can split cells or inject headers.
31:         $value = preg_replace('/[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x7F]/u', '', $value);
32: 
33:         $firstChar = $value[0] ?? '';
34: 
35:         if (in_array($firstChar, self::DANGEROUS_PREFIXES, true)) {
36:             return "'".$value;
37:         }
38: 
39:         return $value;
40:     }
41: }

<file path="app/Support/TwoFactor/TwoFactorManager.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Support\TwoFactor;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\User;
 6: use Illuminate\Support\Str;
 7: use PragmaRX\Google2FA\Google2FA;
 8: 
 9: /**
10:  * Thin wrapper around pragmarx/google2fa that centralizes the two
11:  * operations we actually use: secret generation and code verification.
12:  *
13:  * Recovery codes are just plain strings; we hash them with Laravel's
14:  * Hasher so that a leaked database cannot be used to bypass MFA.
15:  * Hashing is done at generation time; verification uses Hash::check().
16:  */
17: class TwoFactorManager
18: {
19:     public function __construct(
20:         protected Google2FA $google2fa
21:     ) {}
22: 
23:     /**
24:      * Generate a new base32 secret for TOTP.
25:      */
26:     public function generateSecret(): string
27:     {
28:         return $this->google2fa->generateSecretKey();
29:     }
30: 
31:     /**
32:      * Build the otpauth:// URL that authenticator apps consume.
33:      * Encoded as a data URI so it can be rendered in an <img> tag
34:      * without an extra QR service round trip.
35:      */
36:     public function qrCodeDataUri(User $user, string $secret): string
37:     {
38:         $url = $this->google2fa->getQRCodeUrl(
39:             config('app.name', 'Fleet Control'),
40:             $user->email,
41:             $secret,
42:         );
43: 
44:         $writer = new \BaconQrCode\Writer(
45:             new \BaconQrCode\Renderer\ImageRenderer(
46:                 new \BaconQrCode\Renderer\RendererStyle\RendererStyle(220),
47:                 new \BaconQrCode\Renderer\Image\SvgImageBackEnd,
48:             )
49:         );
50: 
51:         $svg = $writer->writeString($url);
52: 
53:         return 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,'.base64_encode($svg);
54:     }
55: 
56:     /**
57:      * Verify a 6-digit TOTP code against the user's secret.
58:      * Allows a window of +/-1 step (30s) to tolerate clock drift.
59:      */
60:     public function verifyCode(string $secret, string $code): bool
61:     {
62:         return (bool) $this->google2fa->verifyKey($secret, $code, window: 1);
63:     }
64: 
65:     /**
66:      * Generate a fresh batch of recovery codes.
67:      *
68:      * @return array{plain: array<int, string>, hashed: array<int, string>}
69:      */
70:     public function generateRecoveryCodes(int $count = 8): array
71:     {
72:         $plain = [];
73:         $hashed = [];
74: 
75:         for ($i = 0; $i < $count; $i++) {
76:             $code = Str::upper(Str::random(5).'-'.Str::random(5));
77:             $plain[] = $code;
78:             $hashed[] = $code;
79:         }
80: 
81:         return ['plain' => $plain, 'hashed' => $hashed];
82:     }
83: }

<file path="app/View/Composers/PendingTransferComposer.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\View\Composers;
 4: 
 5: use App\Enums\TransferStatus;
 6: use App\Models\WarehouseTransfer;
 7: use App\Services\GarageContext;
 8: use Illuminate\View\View;
 9: 
10: /**
11:  * Injects the count of transfers that require action from the
12:  * current garage into the main application layout.
13:  *
14:  * "Requires action" means:
15:  *   - Inbound  + status = dispatched → destination must receive
16:  *   - Outbound + status = disputed   → source must resolve
17:  *
18:  * Drafts and already-received transfers do NOT count — they are
19:  * not pending anyone's attention.
20:  */
21: class PendingTransferComposer
22: {
23:     public function compose(View $view): void
24:     {
25:         $user = auth()->user();
26: 
27:         // Directors operate at company level and have no garage context.
28:         if (! $user || $user->isDirector()) {
29:             $view->with('sidebarPendingTransfers', 0);
30: 
31:             return;
32:         }
33: 
34:         $garageId = GarageContext::resolveGarageId();
35: 
36:         if (! $garageId) {
37:             $view->with('sidebarPendingTransfers', 0);
38: 
39:             return;
40:         }
41: 
42:         $count = WarehouseTransfer::query()
43:             ->visibleToGarage($garageId)
44:             ->where(function ($q) use ($garageId) {
45:                 // Inbound: dispatched, waiting for us to receive.
46:                 $q->where(function ($sub) use ($garageId) {
47:                     $sub->where('to_garage_id', $garageId)
48:                         ->where('status', TransferStatus::Dispatched->value);
49:                 })
50:                 // Outbound: disputed, we (source) must resolve.
51:                     ->orWhere(function ($sub) use ($garageId) {
52:                         $sub->where('from_garage_id', $garageId)
53:                             ->where('status', TransferStatus::Disputed->value);
54:                     });
55:             })
56:             ->count();
57: 
58:         $view->with('sidebarPendingTransfers', $count);
59:     }
60: }

135:         });
136: 
137:         // 4. HTTP EXCEPTIONS (CSRF 419, Throttle 429) — localized JSON
138:         $exceptions->render(function (HttpExceptionInterface $e, Request $request) {
139:             if (! $request->expectsJson()) {
140:                 return null;
141:             }
142: 
143:             $status = $e->getStatusCode();
144:             $message = match ($status) {
145:                 419 => 'Your session has expired. Please refresh the page.',
146:                 429 => 'Too many requests. Please wait a moment.',
147:                 default => $e->getMessage() ?: 'HTTP error',
148:             };
149: 
150:             return response()->json([
151:                 'message' => $message,
152:                 'status' => $status,
153:             ], $status);
154:         });
155: 
156:         // 5. REPORTING
157:         $exceptions->reportable(function (Throwable $e) {
158:             if ($e instanceof ModelNotFoundException
159:                 || $e instanceof NotFoundHttpException
160:                 || $e instanceof AuthorizationException
161:                 || $e instanceof AuthenticationException
162:                 || $e instanceof ValidationException
163:                 || $e instanceof HttpExceptionInterface) {
164:                 return false;
165:             }
166: 
167:             // The app may not be fully booted when this closure runs
168:             // (e.g. an exception thrown during bootstrap itself). Any
169:             // facade call would then fail with "A facade root has not
170:             // been set", masking the original error. Guard against that
171:             // and fall back to PHP's native error_log.
172:             if (! function_exists('app') || ! app()->bound('log')) {
173:                 error_log(sprintf(
174:                     '[Fleet] %s: %s in %s:%d',
175:                     get_class($e),
176:                     $e->getMessage(),
177:                     $e->getFile(),
178:                     $e->getLine(),
179:                 ));
180: 
181:                 return false;
182:             }
183: 
184:             try {
185:                 Log::error($e->getMessage(), [
186:                     'exception' => get_class($e),
187:                     'file' => $e->getFile(),
188:                     'line' => $e->getLine(),
189:                     'request_id' => Illuminate\Support\Facades\Context::get('request_id'),
190:                     'user_id' => auth()->id(),
191:                     'url' => request()?->fullUrl(),
192:                 ]);
193:             } catch (Throwable $loggingFailure) {
194:                 // Logging itself failed — never let it mask the original.
195:                 error_log(sprintf(
196:                     '[Fleet] %s: %s in %s:%d (logging also failed: %s)',
197:                     get_class($e),
198:                     $e->getMessage(),
199:                     $e->getFile(),
200:                     $e->getLine(),
201:                     $loggingFailure->getMessage(),
202:                 ));
203:             }
204:         });
205:     })->create();
</file>

 24:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 25:     | Authentication Guards
 26:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 27:     |
 28:     | Next, you may define every authentication guard for your application.
 29:     | Of course, a great default configuration has been defined for you
 30:     | which utilizes session storage plus the Eloquent user provider.
 31:     |
 32:     | All authentication guards have a user provider, which defines how the
 33:     | users are actually retrieved out of your database or other storage
 34:     | system used by the application. Typically, Eloquent is utilized.
 35:     |
 36:     | Supported: "session"
 37:     |
 38:     */
 39:

 55:     |

 63:

 72:         //     'table' => 'users',

 78:     | Resetting Passwords

 83:     | and the user provider that is invoked to actually retrieve users.
 84:     |
 85:     | The expiry time is the number of minutes that each reset token will be

 89:     | The throttle setting is the number of seconds a user must wait before

 5:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 6:     | Disk Space Thresholds
 7:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 8:     |
 9:     | The health check reports the filesystem as unhealthy when the
10:     | percentage of free space on the storage volume drops below
11:     | `disk_critical_percent`. This is a hard-fail signal — once the
12:     | disk is truly full, Laravel can no longer write sessions, cache,
13:     | logs, or generated PDFs, so an early warning is worth surfacing
14:     | in the monitoring dashboard before the app starts returning 500s.
15:     |
16:     | Default: 5%.
17:     |
18:     */
19:     'disk_critical_percent' => (float) env('HEALTH_DISK_CRITICAL_PERCENT', 5),
20: 
21:     /*
22:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
23:     | Backup Freshness Threshold
24:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
25:     |
26:     | The health check reads the mtime of the freshness marker that the
27:     | backup sidecar touches after every successful dump. If the marker
28:     | is older than this many hours, the app is reported unhealthy — a
29:     | stale backup is a silent data-loss risk that no other probe
30:     | catches.
31:     |
32:     | Default: 25 hours, giving a 1-hour grace window beyond the
33:     | nightly 24-hour backup cadence. Set to 0 to disable the check
34:     | entirely (e.g. in development where there is no backup sidecar).
35:     |
36:     */
37:     'backup_max_age_hours' => (int) env('HEALTH_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS', 25),
38: 
39:     /*
40:     | Path to the freshness marker written by the backup sidecar.
41:     | Read-only bind mount from the host's ./backups directory.
42:     |
43:     | In local development this file usually does not exist, and the
44:     | check is automatically skipped — see HealthController.
45:     */
46:     'backup_marker_path' => storage_path('app/backups/.last-success'),
47: ];

10:     | Example: "5,1" = 5 attempts per minute
11:     |
12:     | These names must match the ones registered in
13:     | AppServiceProvider::registerRateLimiters(). Routes reference
14:     | them via `throttle:<name>`.
15:     |
16:     */

18:     'api' => env('RATE_LIMIT_API', '60,1'),
19:     'pdf' => env('RATE_LIMIT_PDF', '10,1'),
20:     'import' => env('RATE_LIMIT_IMPORT', '5,1'),
21:     'lookup' => env('RATE_LIMIT_LOOKUP', '120,1'),
22: 
23:     /*
24:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
25:     | Login Lockout (web + API email login, PIN login)
26:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
27:     |
28:     | After `attempts` failed attempts, the source is locked out for
29:     | `decay_seconds`. This is NOT a RateLimiter::for() rule — it is
30:     | enforced directly inside LoginRequest using RateLimiter::hit()
31:     | and RateLimiter::tooManyAttempts().
32:     |
33:     */
34:     'login_attempts' => (int) env('RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS', 5),
35:     'login_decay_seconds' => (int) env('RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_DECAY', 900),
36: 
37:     /*
38:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
39:     | PIN Login — Account-Level Lockout
40:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
41:     |
42:     | This limit is IP-independent: it applies to a single employee_code.
43:     | Its purpose is to prevent an attacker who rotates IPs from
44:     | brute-forcing a 4-digit PIN.
45:     |
46:     | 15 attempts * 4-digit space = 15 out of 10,000 combinations.
47:     | That is generous for a real user but unrealistic for an attacker.
48:     |
49:     */
50:     'pin_account_attempts' => (int) env('RATE_LIMIT_PIN_ACCOUNT_ATTEMPTS', 15),
51: ];

<file path="config/sentry.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: /**
 4:  * Sentry configuration for the Fleet Maintenance application.
 5:  *
 6:  * The full set of options is provided by the sentry/sentry-laravel
 7:  * package; this file only declares the values we want to override
 8:  * or that operators are likely to tune per environment.
 9:  *
10:  * Behaviour when SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN is empty (the default):
11:  *   - The Sentry SDK initialises with a null client.
12:  *   - No events are sent anywhere, no network calls are made.
13:  *   - There is effectively zero runtime overhead.
14:  *
15:  * This makes the package safe to ship in every environment: local
16:  * development, CI, and a production deployment that has not yet
17:  * configured Sentry. Operators enable it by setting the DSN in
18:  * .env.production.
19:  */
20: return [
21: 
22:     'dsn' => env('SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN', env('SENTRY_DSN')),
23: 
24:     'release' => env('SENTRY_RELEASE'),
25: 
26:     'environment' => env('SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT', env('APP_ENV', 'production')),
27: 
28:     'sample_rate' => (float) env('SENTRY_SAMPLE_RATE', 1.0),
29: 
30:     'traces_sample_rate' => (float) env('SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE', 0.1),
31: 
32:     'profiles_sample_rate' => (float) env('SENTRY_PROFILES_SAMPLE_RATE', 0.0),
33: 
34:     'send_default_pii' => (bool) env('SENTRY_SEND_DEFAULT_PII', false),
35: 
36:     'attach_stacktrace' => (bool) env('SENTRY_ATTACH_STACKTRACE', false),
37: 
38:     'max_breadcrumbs' => (int) env('SENTRY_MAX_BREADCRUMBS', 50),
39: 
40:     /*
41:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
42:     | before_send — filter noisy / expected events
43:     |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
44:     |
45:     | The application deliberately renders a small set of exceptions as
46:     | normal HTTP responses:
47:     |
48:     |   - GarageAccessDeniedException  → 403 + redirect
49:     |   - StockInsufficientException   → 422 + redirect
50:     |   - MissingGarageContextException → 500 + redirect
51:     |
52:     | These are handled in bootstrap/app.php and are not bugs. Forwarding
53:     | them to Sentry would drown the real signal — a validation error
54:     | from a user is not an incident.
55:     |
56:     | Laravel's reportable() closure in bootstrap/app.php already skips
57:     | these, but adding the filter here too is cheap insurance against a
58:     | future refactor that accidentally reverts the reportable change.
59:     |
60:     */
61:     'before_send' => function (Sentry\Event $event): ?Sentry\Event {
62:         $exceptionsToIgnore = [
63:             App\Exceptions\GarageAccessDeniedException::class,
64:             App\Exceptions\StockInsufficientException::class,
65:             App\Exceptions\MissingGarageContextException::class,
66:             Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException::class,
67:             Illuminate\Auth\AuthenticationException::class,
68:             Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException::class,
69:             Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\ModelNotFoundException::class,
70:             Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\NotFoundHttpException::class,
71:             Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpExceptionInterface::class,
72:         ];
73: 
74:         foreach ($event->getExceptions() as $exception) {
75:             foreach ($exceptionsToIgnore as $ignored) {
76:                 if ($exception instanceof $ignored) {
77:                     return null; // drop the event
78:                 }
79:             }
80:         }
81: 
82:         return $event;
83:     },
84: 
85: ];
</file>

<file path="database/migrations/2026_09_21_111737_ensure_single_super_admin_matches_env.php">
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
 4: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
 5: 
 6: /**
 7:  * Ensures the platform SuperAdmin's email matches the value in
 8:  * SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL.
 9:  *
10:  * Background:
11:  *   Migration 2026_09_07_081048 hard-coded `WHERE email = 'admin@fleet.com'`
12:  *   to promote a user to super_admin. That is fragile in multi-tenant
13:  *   deployments where the SuperAdmin uses a different email.
14:  *
15:  * This migration is idempotent and safe:
16:  *   - If SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL is not set, it does nothing.
17:  *   - If a user with that email exists and is not yet a super_admin,
18:  *     it promotes them.
19:  *   - It never demotes an existing super_admin.
20:  *
21:  * In a fresh installation, UserSeeder already creates the SuperAdmin
22:  * with the correct email, so this migration is a no-op.
23:  */
24: return new class extends Migration
25: {
26:     public function up(): void
27:     {
28:         $email = env('SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL');
29: 
30:         if (empty($email) || ! filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
31:             return; // Nothing to do — no valid email configured
32:         }
33: 
34:         $user = DB::table('users')
35:             ->where('email', $email)
36:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
37:             ->first();
38: 
39:         if (! $user) {
40:             return; // No user with that email — nothing to promote
41:         }
42: 
43:         if ($user->role === 'super_admin') {
44:             return; // Already correct — nothing to do
45:         }
46: 
47:         // We must not create a second super_admin (partial unique index
48:         // users_single_super_admin forbids it). If one already exists,
49:         // log a warning and skip.
50:         $existingSuperAdmin = DB::table('users')
51:             ->where('role', 'super_admin')
52:             ->whereNull('deleted_at')
53:             ->where('is_active', true)
54:             ->where('id', '!=', $user->id)
55:             ->first();
56: 
57:         if ($existingSuperAdmin) {
58:             Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log::warning(
59:                 'SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL points to a user that is not the current SuperAdmin. '
60:                 .'Skipping promotion to avoid violating the single-super-admin rule.',
61:                 [
62:                     'configured_email' => $email,
63:                     'existing_super_admin' => $existingSuperAdmin->email,
64:                 ]
65:             );
66: 
67:             return;
68:         }
69: 
70:         DB::table('users')
71:             ->where('id', $user->id)
72:             ->update(['role' => 'super_admin']);
73: 
74:         Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log::info(
75:             "Promoted user [{$email}] to super_admin via SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL."
76:         );
77:     }
78: 
79:     public function down(): void
80:     {
81:         // Intentional no-op. Rolling back would require us to know
82:         // which super_admin was promoted by this migration, which is
83:         // not tracked. This is a data migration, not a schema change.
84:     }
85: };

39:  * a full scan.

<file path="database/migrations/2026_09_24_101356_fix_composite_unique_indexes_to_partial.php">
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
  4: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
  5: 
  6: return new class extends Migration
  7: {
  8:     /**
  9:      * Replaces the non-partial composite unique constraints created by
 10:      * 2026_09_08_174319 with partial unique indexes that only apply to
 11:      * live rows (deleted_at IS NULL).
 12:      *
 13:      * WHY
 14:      * ---
 15:      * 2026_08_30_140000 established the project-wide convention:
 16:      * uniqueness applies only to non-deleted rows, so a soft-deleted
 17:      * record releases its key for reuse. Every tenant-scoped table in
 18:      * the codebase follows this pattern — companies.slug,
 19:      * garages.code, users.email, users.employee_code, employees.code,
 20:      * bus_brands, service_vehicles, complaint_types, bus_oil_changes.
 21:      *
 22:      * 2026_09_08_174319 then created non-partial composite unique
 23:      * constraints on the SAME columns (buses.garage_id+dqn,
 24:      * buses.garage_id+route_number, warehouses.garage_id+code,
 25:      * drivers.garage_id+code). PostgreSQL keeps both indexes, but the
 26:      * non-partial one is stricter — a soft-deleted row permanently
 27:      * reserves its key, contradicting the reuse semantics that every
 28:      * other table in the application already relies on.
 29:      *
 30:      * CONSEQUENCES BEFORE THIS FIX
 31:      * ----------------------------
 32:      *   - Soft-delete a bus, then re-import the same DQN → unique
 33:      *     violation, even though the import logic intentionally
 34:      *     restores the trashed row.
 35:      *   - Soft-delete a warehouse item, then re-create it with the
 36:      *     same code → unique violation.
 37:      *   - Soft-delete a driver, then re-import the same driver code
 38:      *     → unique violation.
 39:      *
 40:      * WHAT THIS MIGRATION DOES
 41:      * ------------------------
 42:      *   1. Drops the non-partial composite unique constraints.
 43:      *   2. Creates the canonical partial unique indexes with the
 44:      *      "active_unique" suffix that matches the project convention.
 45:      *   3. Removes three stale indexes from 2026_08_30_140000 whose
 46:      *      names still reference the pre-rename column names
 47:      *      (xett_no → route_number, kod → code, kodu → code). They
 48:      *      are functionally redundant after step 2.
 49:      *
 50:      * IDEMPOTENT
 51:      * ----------
 52:      * Every statement is DROP IF EXISTS / CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, so the
 53:      * migration can be re-run on a partially-migrated database.
 54:      */
 55:     public function up(): void
 56:     {
 57:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 58:         // 1. Drop the non-partial composite unique constraints.
 59:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 60:         DB::statement('ALTER TABLE buses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS buses_garage_dqn_unique');
 61:         DB::statement('ALTER TABLE buses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS buses_garage_route_number_unique');
 62:         DB::statement('ALTER TABLE warehouses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS warehouses_garage_code_unique');
 63:         DB::statement('ALTER TABLE drivers DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS drivers_garage_code_unique');
 64: 
 65:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 66:         // 2. Drop the old partial indexes (whose names reference
 67:         //    pre-rename columns) so we can recreate everything with
 68:         //    a single canonical naming convention.
 69:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 70:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS buses_garage_dqn_active_unique');
 71:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS buses_garage_xett_active_unique');
 72:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS warehouses_garage_kod_active_unique');
 73:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS drivers_garage_kodu_active_unique');
 74: 
 75:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 76:         // 3. Create the canonical partial unique indexes.
 77:         // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 78:         DB::statement('
 79:             CREATE UNIQUE INDEX buses_garage_dqn_active_unique
 80:             ON buses (garage_id, dqn)
 81:             WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
 82:         ');
 83: 
 84:         // route_number is nullable — partial index must exclude NULLs
 85:         // explicitly so multiple buses without a route can coexist.
 86:         DB::statement('
 87:             CREATE UNIQUE INDEX buses_garage_route_number_active_unique
 88:             ON buses (garage_id, route_number)
 89:             WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND route_number IS NOT NULL
 90:         ');
 91: 
 92:         DB::statement('
 93:             CREATE UNIQUE INDEX warehouses_garage_code_active_unique
 94:             ON warehouses (garage_id, code)
 95:             WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
 96:         ');
 97: 
 98:         DB::statement('
 99:             CREATE UNIQUE INDEX drivers_garage_code_active_unique
100:             ON drivers (garage_id, code)
101:             WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
102:         ');
103:     }
104: 
105:     public function down(): void
106:     {
107:         // Drop the partial indexes created in up().
108:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS buses_garage_dqn_active_unique');
109:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS buses_garage_route_number_active_unique');
110:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS warehouses_garage_code_active_unique');
111:         DB::statement('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS drivers_garage_code_active_unique');
